title: [RW2] metadata.send feature parity with v1
body:
### Proposal

Recently we [discovered](https://cloud-native.slack.com/archives/C02KR205UMU/p1757928669786829?thread_ts=1749133455.590349&cid=C02KR205UMU) that RW1 flow has a side channel for metadata directly from scrape cache, which completely avoids `metadata-wal-records feature (and its [issues](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/15911)).

PRW1 spec does not contain metadata support, but more users depends on experimental PRW1 support (e.g. Mimir users).

PRW2 has a native, official metadata support in spec. The PRW2 metadata is "connected/attached" to each series we send making it easier to consume. The [PRW1 flow is disabled for PRW2](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/43c1535bdfdd6368d01513459cf5790af8b50f05/storage/remote/queue_manager.go#L538) because of this fundamental difference - old PRW1 metadata were disconnected and per metric family. We can naively use existing `metadataWatcher`.

Instead Prometheus offers (1) `metadata-wal-records` feature and newer (2) `type-and-unit-labels` that allows PRW2 to provide metadata to consumers. (1) has known limitations and overhead, (2) does not support (or plan to) help string, require potentially extra relabelling to strip labels and is generally a new option (not released now).

This issue is to decide what (if anything) should be done to support feature parity around PRW1 metadata flow. 
This is, practically speaking, only required for Mimir users using Prometheus, which is of considerable size.

Some ideas:

A: Focus on (2) `type-and-unit-labels` and provide examples or relabelling for stripping unit and type labels, document the behaviour
B: Implement `metadata.send=true` parity by direct lookup in scrape cache OR a second cache in queue_manager
C:  Mix of (A) and (B) -- only do (B) for help.

title: [RW2]: Prometheus client_golang remote API adoption
body:
### Proposal

Adopt the https://github.com/prometheus/client_golang/tree/main/exp/api/remote from client_golang to replace the current custom remote write handler implementation in Prometheus.

### Context

This proposal is part of the broader https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/16944 outlined in PROM-35. The current Prometheus implementation in storage/remote maintains its own custom protocol handling logic for both v1 and v2 remote write protocols. Meanwhile, the Prometheus team has built an official remote write client in client_golang that does the same thing but is designed to be shared across the ecosystem.


### Benefits

Using the official client means we can share the same remote write implementation with other projects like Mimir, Thanos, and Cortex. It also means protocol updates happen in one place instead of being scattered across different codebases. 

### Potential Concerns

The main concern is that the exp/api/remote package is marked "experimental." However, this refers to the API potentially changing, not the protocol stability. The Remote Write protocol itself is stable - the experimental label just gives flexibility to refine the API before it's locked in (with Prometheus as the core user).

We'd also want to coordinate this with other PRW2.0 work to avoid conflicts.

This leads to partial data ingestion, as only exemplars attached to known series or histograms seem to persisted.

Currently, we return 204 with `X-Prometheus-Remote-Write-Examplars-Written: 0`.

We could solve it by:

## Return 400

Returning 204 for partial write is not compliant, so we could return 400.

## Ingesting the exemplars

In this case, the  `X-Prometheus*` header for exemplars should return `1`.

title: promql: NHCB operations should support different bucket layouts
body:
Currently, `FloatHistogram.Add` (and `.Sub`) methods return an error when called with two histograms containing different custom buckets layouts: https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/5c897e3801ed61e3826484d4b440d931fa12bda0/model/histogram/float_histogram.go#L349-L351

The behaviour can be observed by executing this simple test:
```
# Test native histograms with custom buckets, adding a new bucket.
load 1m
    custom_buckets_histogram{instance="0"} {{schema:-53 sum:3 count:2 custom_values:[5] buckets:[1 1]}}
    custom_buckets_histogram{instance="1"} {{schema:-53 sum:5 count:4 custom_values:[5 10] buckets:[1 2 1]}}

eval instant at 1m sum(custom_buckets_histogram)
    {} {{schema:-53 sum:8 count:6 custom_values:[5] buckets:[2 4]}}
```
- the test fails because of an empty result, also, a warning ("vector contains histograms with incompatible custom buckets (...)") is returned

I believe this limitation is too strict. I would find it way more user friendly if the operation returned a histogram containing all buckets that are present on _both_ histograms. For mismatched buckets (only present on one of the histograms), their values would be rolled up into the next matching (present on both histograms) bucket. There would always exist a matching (catch all) bucket (`+Inf`) for this.

It can be argued that in the most degenerate case (histograms having no common explicit buckets) the resulting histogram would only have the `+Inf` bucket. I believe this behaviour is fine, at least it does not seem to be worse than returning an empty (or partial) response. And I think we should not focus too much on this degenerate case of the users shooting themselves into the foot.

I think the case that deserves more attention is when new buckets are added to existing histograms. After all, one of the selling points of NHCB seems to be low per-bucket overhead, so as a user, I will be tempted to add more buckets in my instrumentation. Likely over several iterations. Likely, with gradual rollouts. Meaning that there will be prolonged periods of time when my queries are affected by this existing limitation.

I believe the solution proposed here works well for cases like this (adding new buckets, but the same would be true for removing some buckets as well) and allows a smooth transition between bucket layouts.

As usual, I might be missing some important detail. @beorn7 I would appreciate your thoughts on this (and I hope it is not too late). Can help with the implementation in case this gets a green light.

title: Add iterator-returning variant of promql.Query engine interface
body:
### Proposal

I'd like to add an extension to the Prometheus engine Go interface that can stream out a result instead of accumulating all series/samples into one [`promql.Result`](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/f4b8840f51bee8afa258e0d4e27fc7fc03358760/promql/value.go#L345)'s giant `parser.Value` as a matrix. 

This would probably use a [go iterator](https://tip.golang.org/doc/go1.23#iterators) though `chan` would be an option too.

## Rationale

This improvement would be useful for the existing `/api/v1/query` and `/api/v1/query_range`. Prometheus could discard the result series and samples as soon as the json serialisation of each one was built, so it doesn't have to accumulate both the whole result vector _and_ the whole json serialisation in memory at once. This can somewhat lower lowers peak memory use for high-cardinality queries, reducing OOM hazards and slow-downs due to forced aggressive go gc runs when approaching `GOMEMLIMIT`s.

The main motivation is to use this in conjunction with the proposed [Streaming Result for Query/QueryRange HTTP API #10040
](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/10040) to allow the client to receive the result without Prometheus having to store the entire final result at all. This can dramatically lower peak memory use for high-cardinality queries and/or range queries with many steps. Even where the query is nontrivial so the executor constructs large interim vectors/matrices during its execution, it still means the final result doesn't have to fit in memory at the same time as the working-memory to create it.

## Limitations

To be clear, none of this fully solves Prometheus's issues with spiky peak memory requirements when serving high cardinality queries. But it'd be a significant step towards that, and would help unlock further improvements as subsequent work on streaming in the executor would have more direct and immediate benefits.

## Implementation

`promql.Query` is used as an interface by other Prometheus engine implementations like https://github.com/thanos-io/promql-engine. Go interfaces do not support default-implementations for methods, so it's generally not reasonable to add methods to an existing interface.

Instead, Go's duck-typing should be used to define a superset-interface like `promql.StreamingQuery` that adds the new method, say `ExecStreaming`.

The PromQL engine implementation of `promql.Query.Exec` could then be implemented in terms of the `promql.StreamingQuery`'s `ExecStreaming`. The underlying [`promql.Engine`](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/11c49151b723099e4616e75926ce5928731c57bd/promql/engine.go#L330-L345)'s [`exec(...)` method 
](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/11c49151b723099e4616e75926ce5928731c57bd/promql/engine.go#L620) and [`execEvalStmt(...)`](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/11c49151b723099e4616e75926ce5928731c57bd/promql/engine.go#L716) would be changed to yield results via an iterator, not [append them to a slice](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/11c49151b723099e4616e75926ce5928731c57bd/promql/engine.go#L772-L789) that is accumulated then returned.

## Concerns

Some testing should be done to determine if there is a meaningful CPU overhead for yielding results through an iterator (or channel, if a channel is selected for the API) instead of appending to a slice. It is expected that this cost will be negligible, and probably more than offset by savings in slice reallocation etc, but this should be tested at least to some extent.

## Related

* https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/10040
* https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/12605
* https://github.com/thanos-io/thanos/issues/7395
* https://github.com/thanos-io/thanos/issues/8487

title: Remote write queue contention causing performance bottlenecks
body: ### What did you do? We are using remote_write to mimir, currently using RW2.0, baseline performance is around 500k samples/sec, running usually with 4 shards (that's our min_shards setting). Sometimes we get the queue backed up, and even significant upsharding to 50 barely increases throughput, at best we saw 650k samples/sec. For testing the max throughput I restarted the remote_write queue by changing its parameters. It usually picked up 5-10 minutes of backlog while rereading the WAL, so it had a lot to churn through. ### What did you expect to see? I would expect a near linear growth for samples/sec with the number of shards, provided we're not capped with cpu or network bandwidth. Cpu usage grew a little bit, but came nowhere near what's available for the process. Network usage is much higher with RW1.0, so we can be certain it's not capped at RW2.0. To make sure we're using multiple tcp connections, we disabled http 2.0. ### What did you see instead? Under which circumstances? Originally we were running with this config ``` queue_config: capacity: 30000 max_shards: 50 min_shards: 4 max_samples_per_send: 10000 batch_send_deadline: 5s min_backoff: 30ms max_backoff: 5s ``` Max throughput peaked at 570k samples/sec. I started suspecting contention by the shards on the WAL because of this part of the `remote_write` documentation: ``` capacity Capacity controls how many samples are queued in memory per shard before blocking reading from the WAL. Once the WAL is blocked, samples cannot be appended to any shards and all throughput will cease. ``` So I increased capacity to 10x max_samples_per_send and that increased our performance: ``` queue_config: capacity: 100000 max_shards: 50 min_shards: 4 max_samples_per_send: 10000 batch_send_deadline: 5s min_backoff: 30ms max_backoff: 5s ``` Max throughput with RW2.0 was around 610k samples/sec To cross check, I tested the same queue config with RW1.0, and it peaked at 880k samples/sec Tried reducing the batch size while keeping capacity: ``` queue_config: capacity: 100000 max_shards: 50 min_shards: 4 max_samples_per_send: 5000 batch_send_deadline: 5s min_backoff: 30ms max_backoff: 5s ``` RW2.0: 520k samples/sec Increased both batch size and capacity: ``` queue_config: capacity: 200000 max_shards: 50 min_shards: 4 max_samples_per_send: 20000 batch_send_deadline: 5s min_backoff: 30ms max_backoff: 5s ``` RW2.0: 580k samples/sec Keep increased capacity, but go back to the original batch size: ``` queue_config: capacity: 200000 max_shards: 50 min_shards: 4 max_samples_per_send: 10000 batch_send_deadline: 5s min_backoff: 30ms max_backoff: 5s ``` RW2.0: 610k samples/sec It looks like there's some serious contention reading the WAL by the shards, which is present in RW1.0, however due to the increased CPU usage of RW2.0, the effect is bigger there. When we run multiple shards, do we run them in different threads? ### System information Linux 6.8.0-1019-aws aarch64 ### Prometheus version ```text prometheus, version 3.5.0 (branch: HEAD, revision: 8be3a9560fbdd18a94dedec4b747c35178177202) build user: root@4451b64cb451 build date: 20250714-16:18:17 go version: go1.24.5 platform: linux/arm64 tags: netgo,builtinassets ``` ### Prometheus configuration file ```yaml remote_write: - url: https://redacted/api/v1/push remote_timeout: 30s write_relabel_configs: - source_labels: [__name__] separator: ; regex: redacted replacement: $1 action: keep protobuf_message: io.prometheus.write.v2.Req

title: PromQL (histograms): counter reset hint (AKA gauge vs. counter) is inconsistent when aggregating native histograms
body:
### What did you do?

Aggregate a number of native histograms with `avg`/`sum` or their `_over_time` versions where those histograms are not all gauge histograms.

This is a relatively rare use case (as you should commonly only aggregate gauge histograms), and the counter reset hint is not heavily used from the user perspective. Thus, I would not let this issue block declaring NH a stable feature, but just consider it a known bug. However, let's aim for fixing it in time. Therefore, marking it as P2 for now.

### What did you expect to see?

A consistent and reproducible handling of those:
1. If all counter reset hints are the same, the result has that same counter reset hint.
2. Otherwise, if there is at least one `GaugeType`, the outcome is `GaugeType`.
3. Otherwise, the outcome is `UnknownCounterReset`.
4. If in any case (except (1)), there is a direct contradiction in the mix (`CounterReset` vs. `CounterReset`), add a warn-level annotation.


### What did you see instead? Under which circumstances?

The aggregation happen in pseudo-random order, and this leads to different outcomes. Furthermore, the avg calculation is using incremental mean calculation, which uses the `Sub` method of the `FloatHistogram`, which always sets the counter reset hint to `GaugeType`.

This results in the following behavior in the cases above:

1. Works for `sum`/`sum_over_time`, but `avg/`avg_over_time` always results in `GaugeType` even if the counter reset hint shared by all involved histograms is a different one.
2. This works already.
3. Works for `sum`/`sum_over_time`, but `avg/`avg_over_time` always results in `GaugeType`.
4. The warn-level annotation is omitted in some cases, because a "lucky" order of aggregation might turn the contradicting counter reset hints into `UnknownCounterReset` or `GaugeType` before they hit their counterpart.

title: instrumentation (of prometheus/prometheus itself): Add native histograms to classic histograms and to complement/replace summaries
body:
https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/16637 made a start here. Quoting/paraphrasing from there:

Now that we have native histograms available, we should probably add native buckets to most of the existing histograms, and ultimately replace most of the summaries by native histograms.

This is broadly the plan: 
- Initially, we cannot really _replace_ the summaries with the histograms because many users would probably like to continue to use the summaries for a while (at least for a smooth transition). So let's have (native) histograms and summaries in parallel for a while, and maybe remove the summaries in v4.
- Existing histograms are easy: We can simply add the native buckets. With v4, we might consider remove or at least reducing the number of classic buckets.
- Problem: We cannot have a summary and a histogram in parallel with the same name. So a newly introduced histogram needs a new name. The current idea of a consistent re-naming scheme is the following: Summary is named `foobar_seconds`. Corresponding histogram is named `foobar_histogram_seconds`. It's not the most elegant thing to add the metric type to the name, but this allow us to apply the same scheme everywhere. (We can consider dropping the `_histogram_` part in v4. But maybe that's not worth the noise.)
- We want to encourage native histogram usage. While we might still add some classic buckets for convenience, let's not use too many of them so that the size of the exposition doesn't blow up. (This is for the newly introduced histograms. Existing classic histograms should be kept as is for now, see above.)

title: instrumentation: remove summaries that have been replaced by native histograms, reduce/remove classic buckets
body:
This is a follow up once #17332 is done, and this is for v4 as it is breaking metrics usage:

- Summaries that got a corresponding native histograms should be removed. (Optional (to be decided): Name the `foobar_histogram_seconds` histogram back to the original name of the summary, i.e. `foobar_seconds`.)
- Remove some or all of the classic buckets of histograms that are now also native histograms. (Don't do this where the classic buckets make sense, e.g. where they are done for specific "magic" boundaries or mirrored from 3rd party histograms.)

title: scrape: Have a static default for `scrape_protocols`
body:
Currently, the default for `scrape_protocols` in the scrape config is set dynamically depending on the (locally effective) setting of `scrape_native_histograms`. This is mostly done so that non-users of native histograms aren't suddenly using protobuf to scrape.

However, this dynamic default is very confusing (to implement and to document). In v4, we should return to a "static" default value for `scrape_protocols`. From the current perspective, that would be a "protobuf first" value, namely `[ PrometheusProto, OpenMetricsText1.0.0, OpenMetricsText0.0.1, PrometheusText1.0.0, PrometheusText0.0.4 ]`. However, by the time v4 drops, we might want to prefer a different list. In any case, the default should just always be the same.

title: `histogram_fraction` returns NaN for classic histograms when `lower` falls within the first bucket
body:
### What did you do?

`histogram_fraction` returns `NaN` when the `lower` argument falls within the first bucket of a classic histogram. For example, for a classic histogram with the following buckets, `histogram_fraction(0.0, 1.5, metric_name)` returns `NaN`, instead of the expected `0.02`. The same query on a native histogram with custom buckets (NHCB) returns the correct result.
```
{
	name:  "positive buckets, lower falls in the first bucket",
	lower: 0.0,
	upper: 1.5,
	buckets: Buckets{
		{UpperBound: 1.0, Count: 1.0},
		{UpperBound: 2.0, Count: 3.0},
		{UpperBound: 3.0, Count: 6.0},
		{UpperBound: math.Inf(1), Count: 100.0},
	},
	// - Bucket [0, 1]: contributes 1.0 observation (full bucket)
	// - Bucket (1, 2]: contributes (1.5-1)/(2-1) * (3-1) = 0.5 * 2 = 1.0 observations
	// Total: (1.0 + 1.0) / 100.0 = 0.02
	expected: 0.02,
	actual: math.NaN(),
},
```

[`BucketFraction`](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/4c1355e14baa60acac0f5d531f79f604ea16da2b/promql/quantile.go#L506), which calculates fractions for classic histograms, always assumes `-Inf` as the lower bound of the first bucket, then tries to interpolate the number of observations within that bucket. This leads to dividing infinity by infinity and thus yields `NaN`. In contrast, [`HistogramFraction`](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/4c1355e14baa60acac0f5d531f79f604ea16da2b/promql/quantile.go#L386), which calculates fractions for native histograms, assumes a lower bound of `0` when the histogram has only positive buckets and produces the correct fraction.

Similarly, for histogram with negative buckets where the first bucket’s lower bound is `-Inf`, `histogram_fraction` returns `NaN` when the `lower` argument falls within that first bucket. For example, for a classic histogram with the buckets below, `histogram_fraction(-4.0, -2.0, metric_name)` returns `NaN` instead of the expected `0.02`.
```
{
	name:  "negative buckets, lower falls in the first bucket",
	lower: -4.0,
	upper: -2.0,
	buckets: Buckets{
		{UpperBound: -3.0, Count: 10.0},
		{UpperBound: -2.0, Count: 12.0},
		{UpperBound: -1.0, Count: 15.0},
		{UpperBound: math.Inf(1), Count: 100.0},
	},
	// - Bucket (-Inf, -3]: contributes zero observations (no interpolation with infinite width bucket)
	// - Bucket (-3, -2]: contributes 12-10 = 2.0 observations (full bucket)
	// Total: 2.0 / 100.0 = 0.02
	expected: 0.02,
	actual: math.NaN(),
},
```
`HistogramFraction` also returns `NaN` in this case.  However, I would expect the first bucket (`-Inf` lower bound) to be treated similarly to the last bucket (`+Inf` upper bound) and contribute no observations. For the last bucket (`+Inf` upper bound), interpolation effectively yields 0 because the denominator is infinite while the numerator is finite:
```
bucket.Count * (value - bucket.LowerBound) / (bucket.UpperBound - bucket.LowerBound)
```
However, if the first bucket has a`-Inf` lower bound, interpolation becomes `∞/∞`, which evaluates to `NaN`, so interpolation should be skipped in this case.


I've explored this issue and think I have a solution. If the maintainers agree this is indeed a bug, I'd be happy to open a PR.



### What did you expect to see?

For histograms with only positive buckets, assume the first bucket's lower bound is `0`. For histograms with negative buckets, no interpolation should be used for the first bucket (`-Inf` lower bound).

### What did you see instead? Under which circumstances?

I saw `NaN` instead.

title: [RW2] Type and unit labels not applied when using Prometheus Agent
body:
Hi! Thanks a lot to the Prometheus team for adding the new `type-and-unit-labels` feature!  

## Related PR
While testing it, i noticed some differences in behavior depending on the Prometheus mode.  

This behavior was tested after applying the changes from [#17329](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/17329).  
While the improvement works correctly in standard Prometheus mode, the following results were observed when using the `agent` mode (details below).

---

##  Observed behavior

### Case 1 - Prometheus scrapes targets directly
Everything works as expected - the `__type__` label appears in the resulting metrics.

**Prometheus config**
```yaml
global:
  scrape_interval: 15s
  scrape_timeout: 10s
  evaluation_interval: 15s

scrape_configs:
  - job_name: 'node-exporter'
    static_configs:
      - targets: ['test-node-exporter:9100']
    relabel_configs:
      - source_labels: [__address__]
        regex: '(.*):(.*)'
        target_label: instance
        replacement: '${1}'
      - source_labels: [__address__]
        regex: '(.*):(.*)'
        target_label: port
        replacement: '${2}'
```

**Prometheus startup flags**
```shell
--enable-feature=type-and-unit-labels,metadata-wal-records
--web.enable-remote-write-receiver
--web.remote-write-receiver.accepted-protobuf-messages=io.prometheus.write.v2.Request
```

**Result**
```shell
[root@exp-01 grizzlybite]# curl -s 'http://192.168.100.7:9090/api/v1/query?query=node_memory_MemAvailable_bytes'  | jq '.data.result[0].metric'

{
  "__name__": "node_memory_MemAvailable_bytes",
  "__type__": "gauge",
  "instance": "test-node-exporter",
  "job": "node-exporter",
  "port": "9100"
}
```

---

### Case 2 - Prometheus Agent sends data via Remote Write v2
When Prometheus runs in **`--agent` mode** and sends metrics through **`remote_write`** using protobuf v2,  
the resulting metrics **do not contain** the `__type__` label - even with the same feature flags enabled.

**Prometheus (receiver)**
```shell
--enable-feature=type-and-unit-labels,metadata-wal-records
--web.enable-remote-write-receiver
--web.remote-write-receiver.accepted-protobuf-messages=io.prometheus.write.v2.Request
```

**Prometheus Agent**
```yaml
remote_write:
  - url: "http://127.0.0.1:9090/api/v1/write"
    protobuf_message: io.prometheus.write.v2.Request
    queue_config:
      max_shards: 40
      capacity: 10000
```

**Agent startup flags**
```shell
--agent
--enable-feature=type-and-unit-labels,metadata-wal-records
```

title: Remote write fails to scale after 3.7 upgrade in some clusters
body:
### What did you do?

I upgraded a few Prometheus instances to from 3.6.0 to 3.7.1.

These instances are spread across the world, and send data to a central instance via remote write.

### What did you expect to see?

title: Support chunked transfer encoding in scraper and parser
body:
### Proposal

Prometheus has to read the whole body of a scrape target's response into memory before starting to parse the data.
This creates a problem where one or more targets with big body response size can significantly increase memory usage on Prometheus (multiply body size by number of targets).
The `body_size_limit` config exists to protect Prometheus from targets that would produce big responses. But it will cause the scrape to fail which is not ideal.

It would be nice if Prometheus supports [Chunked Transfer Encoding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chunked_transfer_encoding) which would allow streaming the scrape data gradually and parse it. Parsed chunks can be discarded to avoid high memory usage by scraper/parser. This would make scraping of targets with big responses possible.

title: Rename CreatedTimestamp (CT) to StartTimestamp (ST)
body:
### Proposal

Following [the DevSummit consensus](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1uurQCi5iVufhYHGlBZ8mJMK_freDFKPG0iYBQqJ9fvA/edit?tab=t.0#bookmark=id.58igluacp6vh) we decided to rename CT feature to ST (StartTimestamp) for consistency with the wider ecosystem, planned storage changes ([PROM-60](https://github.com/prometheus/proposals/pull/60)) and the potential delta temporality ([PROM-48](https://github.com/prometheus/proposals/pull/48))

This issue tracks the renaming work:
- [X] Remote Write 2.0 (not yet stable, so we can change it) ([impl](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/17411), [spec](https://github.com/prometheus/docs/pull/2762))
- [x] Prometheus codebase (https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/17523)
- [x] Prometheus/docs
- [x] PrometheusProto (changing name is non breaking in proto)
- [X] OpenMetrics 2.0 ([PR](https://github.com/prometheus/docs/pull/2770/files))
- [x] Native histogram spec (https://prometheus.io/docs/specs/native_histograms/) cc @krajorama @beorn7 
- [ ] Prometheus SDKs (at least add issue for clients, unlikely we can change some APIs now)

Things that explicitly stay with old naming "created timestamp":
* OpenMetrics 1.0 (will be replaced by 2.0)
* `created-timestamp-zero-ingestion` feature flag (will be renamed or the config moved in the future).

title: promtool: support converting classic histograms queries to native histograms queries
body:
### Proposal

# Background

Currently there is no support in the Prometheus PromQL engine to seamlessly migrate from classic histograms to native histograms. The user needs to rewrite their queries, alerts, recording rules, (dashboards, mixins) to migrate. 

In the  future we might have some seamless solution, possibly built on top of [OTEL schemas](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/otel/schemas/), but for now let's see if we can help with some tooling to make it easier to rewrite/enhance queries.

# References:

* [Specification](https://prometheus.io/docs/specs/native_histograms/#migration-considerations)
* Grafana Mimir [documentation](https://grafana.com/docs/mimir/latest/send/native-histograms/#migrate-from-classic-histograms).
* Related to https://github.com/grafana/mimir/issues/12308

# Requirement

This is just a small first step for a full migration support.

Need promtool cli support and library API support (for downstream projects) for the following:

* Given a classic histograms query and a list of metric names (without magic `_bucket`, `_count`, `_sum` suffixes), return a new query that does the same , but with native histograms.
   For example:
   ```
   histogram_quantile(0.9, sum by (le) (rate(foo_bucket[5m])))
   ```
   to
   ```
   histogram_quantile(0.9, sum (rate(foo[5m])))
   ```
* Given a classic histograms query and a list of metric names return the original query `or`-ed with the native query.
  For example:
  ```
   histogram_quantile(0.9, sum by (le) (rate(foo_bucket[5m])))
   ```
   to
   ```
   (histogram_quantile(0.9, sum by (le) (rate(foo_bucket[5m])))) or (histogram_quantile(0.9, sum (rate(foo[5m]))))
   ```

# Out of scope

There was the question of can we incorporate dashboard variable support, e.g. ?
```
histogram_quantile(0.9, sum by (le) (rate(foo_bucket[$__rate_interval])))
```
or is that too vendor (Grafana/Perses/etc) specific ?

After discussion with @juliusmh , it seems it's best not to try and deal with different kind of variables, but let the vendors deal with the variables. A suggested solution is to apply a reversible substitution algorithm that replaces the variable with something unique so that the PromQL can be parsed and processed and afterwards the process can be reversed.

title: [RW2] type-and-unit-labels not visible when using Prometheus Agent with Prometheus Remote Write v2
body:
Thank you to the Prometheus team for the work on [PR #17387](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/17387)
 adding the new type-and-unit-labels support for Remote Write v2.

I noticed that this PR has been merged recently and decided to test the feature in practice.
However, during testing I found that `__type__` and `__unit__` labels do not appear on the Prometheus Receiver side when metrics are sent via remote_write v2 from Prometheus Agent - even when feature flags are enabled on both ends.

This behavior seems to contradict expectations, and might indicate either a missing configuration detail or a remaining issue in handling metadata through remote write v2.

>Important note:
>I previously opened an issue regarding this behavior, and it was closed as resolved. However, after further >testing, the problem still persists.
>Therefore I am reopening the discussion here with a minimal reproducible configuration below.

### Setup:

#### Prometheus (Receiver) startup flags:
```shell
--config.file=/opt/prometheus/prometheus.yml
--storage.tsdb.path=/mnt/tsdb/prometheus
--web.listen-address=127.0.0.1:9090
--web.enable-remote-write-receiver
--web.remote-write-receiver.accepted-protobuf-messages=io.prometheus.write.v2.Request
--enable-feature=type-and-unit-labels,metadata-wal-records
--log.level=debug
```
#### Prometheus (Agent) startup flags:
```shell
--config.file=/opt/prometheus-agent/prometheus-agent.yml
--agent
--web.listen-address=127.0.0.1:9091
--storage.agent.path=/mnt/tsdb/prometheus-agent
--enable-feature=type-and-unit-labels,metadata-wal-records
--log.level=debug
```
#### Agent configuration
```yaml
global:
  scrape_interval: 15s
  scrape_timeout: 10s

scrape_configs:
  - job_name: 'node-exporter'
    static_configs:
      - targets: ['test-node-exporter:9100']
  - job_name: 'random-data'
    static_configs:
      - targets: ['random-data-exporter:8081']

remote_write:
  - url: "http://127.0.0.1:9090/api/v1/write"
    name: "Remote write to prometheus"
    protobuf_message: io.prometheus.write.v2.Request
```

### Observed behavior

Querying the receiver returns metrics without __type__ and __unit__ labels:
```shell
❯ curl -s 'http://127.0.0.1:9090/api/v1/query?query=node_cpu_seconds_total'  | jq '.data.result[0].metric'
```
```json
{

title: When missing data do not send RESOLVED alerts
body:
### Proposal

Hello, 
I have setup Prometheus-Thanos cluster for monitoring servers(~500 instances).
Cluster contains 2 instances of each component.
I also have 2 Alertmanager instances that are in cluster.

Problem is that i have a lot of alerts, and i always have some alerts firing, so i am fixing them one by one. 
When there is some connectivity problem and prometheus do not receive data for alert that is firing it is sending RESOLVED notification which is not true.

I understand that this is default behaviour for Prometheus, but it is false positive and could result in wrong decisions.

It would be nice to have some configuration option when writing an alert to setup something like No Data ->  Keep Last State (feature on Grafana).
This feature will allow us to tell Prometheus to keep alert firing if there is no data received, because we can set another alert for target status, no data, etc.. There is no reason to receive resolved when alert is not resolved.

My logic is:

mem_used_percent > 80

value 70 -> alert firing

no value -> resolved 

As you can see we receive resolve for no data, not for real value. 
Alert should be resolved only if value is above threshold. No data is no data. 

This can be really hard to manage, you need to find workarounds with Alertmanager inhibitions to silence some resolved alerts if another for no data is active or something like that. Imagine someone who is just starting with this services...

Best Regards!

title: [lookback-delta] alert is fake firing
body:
Currently, my Prometheus query_lookback_delta is set to 61 minutes, and a key metric has a scrape_interval of 1 hour.

Here is the issue:

At time T, an alert starts firing.

If I remove the problematic target at any time between T and T+1h, the alert continues to fire.

Only after T+1h (when the last valid sample falls outside the 61-minute query_lookback_delta window), does Prometheus stop seeing the metric and the alert resolves.

This creates an unnecessary delay in alert resolution. What can I do to make the alert resolve immediately after I remove the target?

title: Stabilize feature flag `extra-scrape-metrics`
body:
The feature flag has been around for 4 years already, so I'd like to start discussing what needs to be done to stabilize the feature :) 

When enabled, the feature flag will cause Prometheus to expose extra metrics **per-target**. Those metrics are important for monitoring scrape performance, but on instances with several targets, they can cause high-cardinality issues.


Some heads-up, my motivation here is stabilizing this feature on the otel-collector side https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/44181

title: Scrape commit duration observability
body:
### Proposal

### Problem Statement

Motivated by https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/issues/44197.  Somewhat related to https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/13647.

We (the opentelemetry collector's prometheus receiver) would like to be able to measure the latency from the time that a scrape was initiated to when Commit() has completed. Someone on the call from Alloy said that they separately measure the latency of Collect() but I haven't confirmed that.

I'm opening an issue here because solving this in Prometheus would help keep the monitoring + debugging experience more consistent, and would potentially benefit Prometheus users as well.

Today, the `scrape_duration_seconds` metric includes everything except `Commit()` and `Rollback()` (since defer statements are evaluated in reverse order of their definition): https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/1174b0ce4f1f302b96bc0dcc1112e142801b5eb1/scrape/scrape.go#L1428-L1444

### Proposed Solution

Change `scrape_duration_seconds` to include Commit().  In practice, I don't expect this to be a noticeable change for users, as the metric is still likely dominated by the time required to make the HTTP request.

Downsides:

* This changes the definition of a metric that is widely used. Might be considered breaking, and therefore not acceptable until the next major version.
* Commit is not affected by the scrape timeout. It might be confusing to users that scrape_duration_seconds can exceed scrape_timeout_seconds without triggering a timeout.
    * However, this is also the case for parsing the response and calling Append(), so this isn't really a change from the current state.

### Alternatives Considered

#### Introduce scrape_commit_duration_seconds

It would just measure the duration of Commit(). This could be part of --enable-feature=extra-scrape-metrics.

Downsides:

* Low Value: The duration of commit is likely to be very small, and not very meaningful on its own. It is unlikely to be useful for debugging scrape timeouts or delayed scrape intervals unless something was very, very wrong.
* Hard to compute end-to-end latency: Unless i'm mistaken, it would be hard to compute a percentile for `scrape_duration_seconds` + `scrape_commit_duration_seconds` to determine the overall latency, which is the stated goal of the issue.

#### Introduce a scrape commit metric in the collector

We could simply measure the scrape commit duration in our Appender implementation. This has the same downsides as scrape_commit_duration_seconds, but additionally would not be shared between the two projects.

title: promqltest: Allow testing of native histogram counter reset hint
body:
The promql testing framework already allows specifying a counter reset hint in a native histogram that is part of the expected result. However, the counter reset hint is then not compared with the one in the actual result.

Example of a test specifying a counter reset hint (which isn't really tested):
https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/a66c696530e2305566c74871d0509b9fa9c502ac/promql/promqltest/testdata/native_histograms.test#L1110-L1115

This is probably not as easy as adding this comparison. Ideally, we could implement a semantics where not specifying the counter reset hint means "I don't care about the counter reset", while an explicitly specified counter reset hint means "please check this". Otherwise, we have to rework all tests to explicitly specify the hint, as long as it is not the default (which is `counter_reset_hint:unknown`).

title: tsdb/agent: Prevent unread segments from being truncated
body:
### Proposal

Today the tsdb/agent truncates the the WAL segments based on the assumption,
https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/f50ff0a40ad4ef24d9bb8e81a6546c8c994a924a/tsdb/agent/db.go#L676 which is not verified before truncation occurs.

Due to this it's really hard to determine how much downtime can be tolerated in a remote write configuration since it's a factor of `TruncateFrequency` + rate of data in. This leads to a much higher`TruncateFrequency`than is really necessary and much larger WALs that must be fully replayed on startup. Internally we run with a 15 minute interval as we are okay with trading off downtime tolerance for less memory usage.

I would propose `remote.Storage` expose the ability to subscribe to be notified when a segment changes. This would be called after all current queues have read past a segment, [sample implementation](https://github.com/grafana/prometheus/compare/staleness_disabling_v3.4.2...kgeckhart:prometheus:kgeckhart/wlog-propogate-read-segments).

After segment notifications are working the tsdb/agent could subscribe and truncate based on segments that have been fully read. At this point we could consider dropping the default `TruncateFrequency` allowing for smaller WALs. 

I'm not sure how much of this, if any, is applicable for the tsdb proper

title: tsdb/agent: Checkpoint based on Series in Memory
body:
### Proposal

The agent currently uses the same Checkpoint implementation as all other parts of prometheus, https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/61aa82865d9c8474393bbbdcd539c58f63ba514f/tsdb/wlog/checkpoint.go#L87-L90 
The checkpoint serves three purposes for agent mode,
1. Populates the agent db `stripeSeries` with known series + last sample timestamps on startup
2. Populate series caches in queue_manager on startup
3. Pruning the series caches in queue_manager after a new checkpoint is created 
4. _Not applicable for agent mode yet and might be dropped_ Most recently metadata for a series

This is an incredibly small subset of the data vs what is persisted in a checkpoint which includes, series which exist in the WAL, samples above mint, float and regular histogram samples above mint, exemplars above mint, and latest metadata. In order to create a checkpoint with all these records we re-read the current checkpoint + all segments. This is a lot of overhead given all the data we require for the checkpoint is currently in memory between `stripeSeries` and the deleted series in agent db.

I propose we introduce another checkpoint implementation which could look something like,
```go
type ActiveSeries interface {
    Ref() chunks.HeadSeriesRef
    Labels() labels.Labels
    LastSampleTimestamp() int64
}

// Checkpoint creates an unindexed checkpoint containing record.RefSeries and 
// record.RefSample for ActiveSeries and  a record.RefSeries for the recentlyDeleted series. 
func Checkpoint(logger *slog.Logger, w *WL, seriesIter iter.Seq[ActiveSeries], recentlyDeleted []chunks.HeadSeriesRef)
```
that could be driven by the data we currently have in memory which would,
1. Reduce the overhead of taking a checkpoint
2. Reduce the overhead of queue_manager reading a checkpoint as checkpoints will be smaller
3. Improve startup times/resource usage due to smaller checkpoint sizes

I did a [quick implementation](https://github.com/grafana/alloy/compare/main...kgeckhart/segment-tracking-new-checkpoint-and-replay#diff-f8404620b6d8190ba878e405a75ea5b9989163caa46892e98e05afb99ce3d519) of this in Grafana Alloy where it shrunk a 214MB checkpoint by 56% down to 137MB, with the following improvements to creating a checkpoint + loading a checkpoint
```

```

title: metadata: Move caching from scrapeCache.metadata to head.series
body:
### Proposal

As discussed on https://cloud-native.slack.com/archives/C06B8KJUU2Y/p1763451934229489 and https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/17436 we would love to have an experiment where we only cache metadata in memory once in memSeries in head, instead of the scrape caches.

Related to https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/17191

### Rationales

* While `type-and-unit-labels` feature help with the id of metric and type and unit storage (labels), it's still experimental, it leaks to consumption (i.e PromQL for better or worse) and it does not support metric help.
* Metadata is still used by Metadata APIs and RW1. Users expressed the need to ensure [similar use with RW2 too](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/17191). For RW2 (and generally better experience on consumption), we need metadata to be be per series not per metric family.
* `metadata-wal-records` is expensive and is planned to be deprecated. `type-and-unit-labels` is one replacement, but has limitations. No other good replacements other than longer term plans with Parquet.
* We already have logic to store metadata in memSeries, we already pay some cost for extra *metadata.Metadata field. This logic is only for `metadata-wal-records` as of now.
* Metadata caching was crucial for detecting changes for `metadata-wal-records` but it's trivial to detect those on head already if we store things in memSeries, especially with the unified appender https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/17610/

With all of this, even with persistent metadata one day with Parquet, it would make sense to improve metadata caching. @pipiland2612 already explored some of this path with https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/17436 (using memSeries metadata, without moving fully), but there will be extra overhead UNLESS we move the metadata fully from the scrape cache to head.

### Solution Details

To avoid races (records for series in WAL exists, but metadata is not yet cached in mem), we likely need to store metadata when we create / get memSeries in Append without waiting for the commit, similar to how we store labels.

To derisk, this could be behind a feature flag.

Queue manager in this scenario would use head for metadata (and series!) lookups, no need to decode any records. This would apply to agent mode too.

For current metadata uses (API and RW1), we likely need to build extra mapping `map[metricFamilyName]HeadSeriesRef` likely in head and likely store mfName on memSeries 🙃  l
* For [Metadata API ](https://prometheus.io/docs/prometheus/latest/querying/api/#querying-metric-metadata) new flow will be faster, no need to talk to scrape targets.
* For RW1 same, no need for scrape targets, straight to head potentially.
* For [TargetMetadata API](https://prometheus.io/docs/prometheus/latest/querying/api/#querying-target-metadata) it will be a bit more expensive, but perhaps acceptable, it's not often used (?). We would use `map[metricFamilyName]HeadSeriesRef` for [GetMetadata](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/main/scrape/target.go#L127) or scrapeCache.series/scrapeCache.seriesCur for [ListMetadata](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/e7999528fab9a2668bfb2b6cb1394dc11c06c54c/scrape/target.go#L94)

Long term, metadata per mfName could be replaced (4.0?) to per series and be a bit simpler.

Lot's of unknowns, especially around metadata API use, and how it affects lock contention for memSeries (is it not too heavily accessed), but perhaps worth a try?

cc @krajorama @kgeckhart @bboreham

title: OR should not take ignoring() / on()
body:
### What did you do?

PromQL has the `or` operator - https://prometheus.io/docs/prometheus/latest/querying/operators/#logicalset-binary-operators.

I can write `foo or bar` and the query will return `foo` if there are any results for it, if there are none then it will return whatever `bar` returns.

But `or` being a binary operator also supports `on(...)` and `ignoring(...)`, which Prometheus  will happily accept:

```
foo or on(xxx) bar
```

```
foo or ignoring(xxx) bar
```

The problem is that such query would make very little sense - if there are no results for `foo` then it cannot possibly be matched with `bar` on any label.
In practice the usage of `on(...)` or `ignoring(...)` doesn't seem to do anything and the query does the exact same thing. But it seems confusing to allow this no-op clause in PromQL.

### What did you expect to see?

`OR` shouldn't allow `on()` or `ignoring()`

### What did you see instead? Under which circumstances?

PromQL accepts `on()` or `ignoring()` for `OR` but it doesn't seem to do anything

title: storage: Switch to unified, transactional AppenderV2 API; remove Appender.
body:
### Delivery

> Putting delivery section on top for a clear status, see proposal below.

https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/17610 is the "preview" PR with all changes so far. Once buildable, we can prombench and see the effects (e.g. import from downstream code).

#### M1

* [x] *PART1*: Add `AppenderV2` interface; add TSDB implementation (next to `Appender`): https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/17629
* [x]  *PART2*: Refactor scrape package; add adapters for multi version of Appender use: https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/17631
* [x]  *PART3*: Add `AppenderV2` interface to TSDB Agent https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/17677
* [x]  *PART4*: Switch OTLP, RW receiving: 
   * [x] https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/17834
   * [x] https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/17835
   * [x] OTLP https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/17990
   * [x] OTLP https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/17992
   * [x] https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/17996
   * [ ] 
* [x] Switch scrape to use  `AppenderV2` fully, allow Appender mode for importers (e.g. Otel).
  * [x] https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/17867
  * [x] https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/17872
  * [x] https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/17976
  * [x] https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/17978

* [ ] Swich rule-manager 
* [ ] Switch everything else (e.g. promqltest etc).
* [ ] Understand the impact for Thanos, Mimir, Cortex, Otel (upgrade PRs on those repos).
* [x] Migrate Otel collector `prometheusreceiver` to `AppenderV2`.
    * [WIP](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-collector-contrib/pull/45597); initial feedback is that [AppenderV2 helps a lot](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/17872#issuecomment-3787022807).

#### M2

* [ ] Remove storage.Appender (deprecate first with a clear ETA e.g. Q2 2026). Not removing/delaying means supporting unused ~10k LOC with tests.

### Proposal

Mentioned in various discussions ([OTLP CombinedAppender](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/16951/files#r2256396176), [early PR](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/17104), [PROM-60](https://github.com/prometheus/proposals/pull/60), [Slack](https://cloud-native.slack.com/archives/C01AUBA4PFE/p1764149599582409)), but this deserves a dedicated issue.

We propose a replacement to our existing [`storage.Appender`](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/b0649e08c4391c68009266779154adc72085d8cc/storage/interface.go#L262) in a form of  `storage.AppenderV2` that is:
* simpler (3 vs 9 methods).
* have transactional exemplars, metadata and ST attachments
* allow extensibility with hybrid param + struct parameters
* efficient enough
* is not breaking Prometheus binary guarantees/behaviour.

*No feature flag is planned, given complexity of supporting both paths for the whole codebase, plus  it should not break Prometheus users.*

We propose to add dual appender v2 path to `scrape` and `TSDB/agent` only. Rest of the code switches to v2 atomically (PR). Once Prometheus switches fully to v2 we then remove v1:
* From `scrape` the moment we got ack from Otel/Alloy for moving to v2.
* From `TSDB/agent` the moment we got ack from Cortex/Thanos/Mimir/Alloy.

title: created-timestamp-zero-ingestion spams logs with WARN on ongoing metrics
body:
### What did you do?

Enabled created-timestamp-zero-ingestion feature. Related to #16951 

WARNs for every single ongoing metric, every single time they are reported:
```
time=2025-12-03T09:51:41.654Z level=WARN source=combined_appender.go:158 msg="Error when appending CT from OTLP" component=web err="too old sample" series="{__name__=\"blabla\", client=\"blabla\", \"client_service.namespace\"=\"blabla\", connection_type=\"database\", failed=\"false\", le=\"0.1\", server=\"blabla\"}" created_timestamp=1764754661141 timestamp=1764755501143 sample_type=float
```

It seems to want to create the zero sample at `created_timestamp=1764754661141`, which is outside the `outOfOrderTimeWindow` setting and thus a WARN is given.



### What did you expect to see?

`AppendCTZeroSample` is STILL called, either with the earliest possible time allowed by the `outOfOrderTimeWindow` setting (the assumption being that the metric is reported way too late) OR the sample timestamp (the assumption being that prometheus was down at the time of creation and this is the earliest time it could be reported).
NOT recording a zero just because the timestamp is too old changes the semantics of the metric and thus makes it unreliable.

### What did you see instead? Under which circumstances?

WARN every single time the metric is reported

title: Allow users to use lookback_delta in the query itself
body:
### Proposal

# Context
  Everyone familiar with Prometheus is aware of lookback period and how it affects queries. We have to be aware of the issue it causes with 'step' in range selector, with the biggest issue being data duplication.
  
Some examples of lookback period causing issues/confusion:
1. https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/17079
2. https://groups.google.com/g/prometheus-users/c/6P8HKo5fB5Y

My company uses Prometheus for IoT data, which means that disconnects are a real concern. If there is a 3min period of "missing data", we want to be able to easily capture this 3 minutes in our query. Which is not easy if our lookback delta is always 5m.

# The problem
To keep it succinct, for a default `5min` lookback_delta...
1. If `step < 5m `, the last data point gets 'duplicated/repeated'
2. If `step > 5m`, then some data might be lost as it was not caught in the lookback period.
3. If `step == lookback` delta, then there is no data duplication or data loss.

# Proposal
Please allow users to put lookback_delta in range selector in the format `[time_range:step:lookback_delta]`.

For example, 
```
metric_A{labels} [1d:10m:10m]
```
will return metric data for 1 day, at 10 minutes interval, with 10 minutes lookback period.

Advanced use case:
```
aggr2_over_time(aggr_over_time(metric_A{labels} [1h:10m:10m]) [1d:1h:1h])
```
^Please note that this example provides 2 lookback_deltas in 1 query. The inner function uses a lookback delta of 10m while the outer function uses a lookback delta of 1h.

Thanks for reading and I hope you will consider this for implementation.

title: Add Certificate-Based OAuth Support for Azure AD Remote Write
body:
### Proposal

Currently, Prometheus OSS supports Azure AD authentication for remote write using either:

- Client secret (OAuth client credentials)
- Managed identities (system or user-assigned)
- Workload identity

However, it **does not support certificate-based OAuth authentication**

In Azure, Entra ID app registrations allow clients to authenticate using **a client certificate instead of a client secret**. This provides:

- Stronger security (private keys vs plain-text secrets)
- Automatic rotation possibilities
- Compliance with enterprise security policies

At the moment, the only way to use certificate-based authentication with Prometheus remote write is via the **Microsoft sidecar**, which proxies requests and handles certificate auth externally. This introduces extra operational complexity and prevents native Prometheus integration with Azure AD certificate auth and the sidecar is on the path for deprecation.

---

### Proposed change

- Introduce a new configuration block `azuread.certificate` for remote write:

```yaml
remote_write:
  - url: https://<dce>/api/v1/write
    azuread:
      cloud: AzurePublic
      certificate:
        client_id: <APP_ID>
        tenant_id: <TENANT_ID>
        certificate_file: /etc/prometheus/certs/app.crt
        private_key_file: /etc/prometheus/certs/app.key
```

### Implementation Details

- Implement a new credential path in `azuread.go`:
  - If the `certificate` configuration is provided, use `azidentity.NewClientCertificateCredential` to fetch tokens.
  - Inject the resulting bearer token into the remote write requests (same as the current OAuth client secret path).
  - Maintain existing behavior for client-secret, managed identity, and workload identity authentication paths.
  - Add validation to ensure only **one Azure AD auth method** is configured at a time.

### Benefits

- Native Prometheus support for certificate-based OAuth.
- Eliminates the need for a sidecar container for certificate authentication.
- Enables enterprise security standards that require certificate-based authentication.
- Backwards-compatible with existing client secret and managed identity configurations.

I am happy to implement this feature and contribute it to the Prometheus project.

title: Feature Request: Add Labelmap PromQL Function
body:
# Summary

Add a PromQL function for labelmap available during querying with a similar behavior to the `labelmap` action in the relabel config.


# Explanation

Currently, PromQL supports the `label_replace()` function, which is an incredibly useful function in manipulating labels during querying for compatibility reasons and to allow for better aggregation.

With that said, there is currently no way to preform that renaming for a group of labels. The `label_replace()` requires a source label and a destination label - meaning it is bound to a single replacement.

In the case where multiple replacements are needed, the only available solution is to nest these functions one within the other. Apart from increasing the complexity of the query and reducing readability, this approach fails when the labels we wish to manipulate are not fixed or dynamic. 

Currently, there is **no way** to manipulate **a changing set of labels** at the querying level.

# Solution

Prometheus already offers a great solution to a nearly identical problem during relabeling: the `labelmap` action.

We propose to add a PromQL function which acts exactly like the relabel action.

Note that this idea is a somewhat mix between the classic `labelmap` action and the `label_replace()` function.

This approach is simple, and in-short, copies the `labelmap` action behavior to a usable PromQL function. It syntax goes as follows:

`labelmap(query, regex, replacement)`

1. `query` defines the PromQL query being manipulated.

2. `regex` defines the **label name** of the labels being manipulated. Only labels matching said regex are affected. 

3. `replacement` defines the new **label name** used for each affected label. Supports regex capture groups.

### Example:

Assume the following PromQL query:
`up{job="kubernetes_pods"}`

Returns the following series:

`up{job="kubernetes_pods", kubernetes_cluster="cluster1", kubernetes_namespace="namespace1", kubernetes_pod="pod1"}`

`up{job="kubernetes_pods", kubernetes_cluster="cluster2", kubernetes_namespace="namespace2", kubernetes_pod="pod2"}`

`up{job="kubernetes_pods", kubernetes_cluster="cluster3", kubernetes_namespace="namespace3", kubernetes_pod="pod3"}`

Notice many of the label names start with `kubernetes`. For this example, we'd want to drop that prefix from all relevant labels.

Disclaimer: although this is possible to do permanently during relabeling, saving it like that is not always desired and irreversible - unlike a PromQL function, which is relevant only for a specific query.

If we surround our query with the new `labelmap` function as follows:

`labelmap(up{job="kubernetes_pods"},"kubernetes_(.+)", "$1")`

We get as a result the following:

`up{job="kubernetes_pods", cluster="cluster1", namespace="namespace1", pod="pod1"}`

`up{job="kubernetes_pods", cluster="cluster2", namespace="namespace2", pod="pod2"}`

`up{job="kubernetes_pods", cluster="cluster3", namespace="namespace3", pod="pod3"}`

Notice how the `job` label is unaffected.

This way, we achieve an almost identical behavior to the relabel action, while preserving the flexibility a PromQL function offers.

# Benefits

1. The best of both worlds: add supports for dynamic “label renaming” that the `labelmap` action offers while preserving the flexibility the `label_replace()` function has.
2. Familiar concept: simple and relies on existing behavior.
3. Offers a solution for a use case currently unavailable when querying.

We would love to hear more thoughts on the matter, and hope (if eligible) to see it implemented in the near future!

title: Support for dedicated HTTP probe port in Prometheus (node_exporter, pushgateway, alert_manager, Kubestate_metrics) with mTLS or Basic Auth enabled (i.e. for node exporter)
body:
### Proposal

### Feature Request

Currently, when mTLS or Basic Authentication is enabled in `Prometheus`, all endpoints (including metrics and probes) must be accessed securely, which limits the ability to perform health or liveness probes using plain HTTP. 

**Proposed Enhancement**
Introduce support for a dedicated HTTP port in `Prometheus` that serves only probe or status endpoints, independent of the main HTTPS port. This design would allow HTTP-based health probes to function even when the primary metrics endpoint is protected by mTLS or Basic Auth. The probe port would:
- Be explicitly configurable.
- Serve only minimal endpoints like `/healthz` or `/ready`.
- Remain isolated from any metrics or authenticated resources to maintain security boundaries.

**Use Cases**
- Kubernetes deployments where secure metrics scraping is enforced via mTLS but liveness probes must remain lightweight (HTTP).
- Environments using Basic Auth where probe requests should bypass authentication.
- Scenarios requiring explicit HTTP probe endpoints for infrastructure or cloud-native monitoring tools.

**Benefits**
This change would improve the operational flexibility of secure Prometheus deployments without compromising security, by cleanly separating health-check traffic from metrics collection.

title: info() function returns empty when filtering by label that already exists on input vector
body:
The experimental info() PromQL function returns no results when the info-selector filters by a label that already exists on the input vector, even when that label exists on target_info with a matching value.

## Steps to Reproduce

Given OTLP metrics with resource attributes that result in:

Metric:
postgresql_commits_total{host_name="orbstack", instance="postgresql/postgres", job="postgresql"}

target_info:
target_info{host_name="orbstack", instance="postgresql/postgres", job="postgresql", service_name="postgresql", ...}

Note: host_name is promoted to the metric via promote_resource_attributes, so it exists on both the metric and target_info.

Queries and results:

# Works - no filter
info(postgresql_commits_total)
# ✓ Returns enriched metrics

# Works - filter by label only on target_info
info(postgresql_commits_total, {service_name="postgresql"})
# ✓ Returns enriched metrics

# FAILS - filter by label that exists on BOTH metric and target_info
info(postgresql_commits_total, {host_name="orbstack"})
# ✗ Returns empty

info(postgresql_commits_total, {host_name=~".+"})
# ✗ Returns empty

## Expected Behavior

All queries should return results. The info-selector filters which target_info series to consider. Since a matching target_info exists, the join should succeed regardless of whether the filter label also exists on the input metric.

## Actual Behavior

When the info-selector includes a label that already exists on the input vector, info() returns no results.

## Workaround

Filter on the metric directly, use info() selector only for labels exclusive to target_info:

info(postgresql_commits_total{host_name=~"$host_name"}, {service_name="postgresql"})

title: LFX Mentorship: Improving Documentation for Prometheus and OpenTelemetry Interoperability
body:
## What the mentorship will explore

During the [March–May 2025 LFX mentorship cohort](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/15909), we conducted UX research to understand user challenges around how Prometheus handles OpenTelemetry resource attributes. One key finding was that users struggled to find clear, cohesive, and practical documentation explaining how the two systems work together.

This issue proposes continuing that work by tackling the documentation gaps problem as part of the March 2026 LFX mentorship term.

## What we look for in candidates

We’re looking for contributors who:

- Are interested in technical writing, documentation, or developer experience
- Enjoy breaking down complex technical concepts into clear, approachable explanations
- Want to contribute to and be a part of the Prometheus community, with an understanding that documentation is an ongoing responsibility rather than a one-off contribution

> Prior expertise in Prometheus or OpenTelemetry is **not required**, but a willingness to learn and actively engage with both communities is important.

## Expected outcome of the mentorship

- Review and audit existing Prometheus and OpenTelemetry documentation related to interoperability
- Define a prioritized documentation improvement plan together with the mentors.
- Concrete documentation improvements submitted upstream, such as conceptual explanations, practical guides, examples, diagrams, and cross-project references.
- Establish basic criteria or methods to evaluate documentation effectiveness during the mentorship.

## Resources

To get started, applicants are encouraged to:

- Familiarize themselves with Prometheus and OpenTelemetry at a high level
- Review [outputs from the previous UX mentorship](https://github.com/prometheus-community/ux-research/tree/main/prom-otel-research), including [interviews](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLK87GQAYMTgM9Q5vjz7gIp8hW0o53FubD) and [blog posts](https://opentelemetry.io/blog/2025/ux-research-prometheus-otel/)
- Check out existing documentation:

   - https://opentelemetry.io/docs/languages/js/exporters/#prometheus (This is JavaScript-specific, but all languages have a similar page)

body: ### Proposal Hello :) Thank you for this awesome project! For alerting use cases, we often want to be alerted if an error/retry happens more than N times, as we then assume that the automatic retry failed. E.g. `increase(cilium_errors_warnings_total[5m]) > 3` We have the situation that error/retry metrics only get created when the first errors/retries are encountered, e.g. `cilium_errors_warnings_total{kubernetes_pod_name="cilium-xyz", subsystem="fqdn/dnsproxy"} = 5`. The first value of this metric is then e.g. 5 and has no prior 0 value, which results in the increase function producing values between 1 and 2.33 in the next minutes. This results in us missing the first threshold breaching event. I understand, that this is the expected behavior, as it cannot be assumed, that the metric started at 0. As we have this type of metric behavior in multiple places, I think we could benefit from a query function that **does** assume, that the metric was 0 before. E.g. `increase_assume_zero_start(cilium_errors_warnings_total[5m])` returns either the only sample value in the time, or a normal `increase` calculation. That way, we would receive a spike to 5 for our example, and the alert would trigger. We can already somewhat reproduce this behavior with this very verbose (and slow?) query ``` ( last_over_time(cilium_errors_warnings_total[5m]) ) and ( count_over_time(cilium_errors_warnings_total[5m]) == 1 ) or ( increase(cilium_errors_warnings_total[5m]) ) and ( count_over_time(cilium_errors_warnings_total[5m]) > 1 ) ``` or with experimental functions enabled: ``` ( last_over_time(cilium_errors_warnings_total[5m]) ) and ( count_over_time(cilium_errors_warnings_total[5m]) == 1 ) or ( last_over_time(cilium_errors_warnings_total[5m]) - first_over_time(cilium_errors_warnings_total[5m]) ) and ( count_over_time(cilium_errors_warnings_total[5m]) > 1 ) ``` The second option also has the benefit of producing pure integer results for counter increases, as it is not performing interpolation. But that would definitely need a different name than `increase`, as it differs too much in behavior. So ideally, 3 new functions: * an increase variant, that assumes that a metric was at 0 at the beginning of the time range, if no samples exist there * a delta function without extrapolation * a delta function without extrapolation, that assumes that a metric was at 0 at the beginning of the time range, if no samples exist there Is this something, you can see the use-case for? We encountered this issue for multiple metrics from multiple services in the past.

title: Improve TypeScript typings for global jQuery and moment usage in React UI
body:
### Background

In `web/ui/react-app/src/globals.ts`, jQuery and moment are intentionally attached to the global `window` object to support existing UI code and third-party dependencies.

At the moment this is implemented using `any` casts with ESLint disables, for example:

    (window as any).jQuery = jquery;
    (window as any).moment = require("moment");

This works correctly at runtime, but it weakens type safety and requires suppressing lint rules, which makes the global dependencies less explicit to contributors working on the React UI.

---

### Proposal

I propose replacing the `any` casts with explicit TypeScript typings for these global variables by extending the `Window` interface.

This would allow us to:

- Keep the current runtime behavior unchanged
- Remove the need for `any` and ESLint disable comments
- Make existing global dependencies explicit at the type level
- Improve overall type safety and developer experience in the React UI

---

### Scope

- Limited to the React UI (`web/ui/react-app`)
- No behavioral or API changes
- Focused only on typing improvements for existing global assignments

If this approach sounds reasonable, I’d be happy to open a PR implementing it.

title: WAL corruption stops compaction indefinitely causing unbounded disk growth beyond retention window
body:
### Proposal

# Description
I have a small home server running prometheus and I noted a strange behaviour.

When a WAL segment becomes corrupted, Prometheus logs the corruption and continues running, serving queries normally.
However, WAL compaction for that segment (and all subsequent segments) stops permanently.

This leads to a situation where:
- Prometheus appears healthy and continues ingesting data.
- WAL compaction no longer progresses.
- Retention enforcement is effectively blocked.
- Disk usage grows without bound.

In practice, once the data in the corrupted segment is older than the configured retention period, there is no remaining value in preserving it. Yet the compactor remains blocked forever, requiring manual operator intervention to remove WAL data.

# Desired behaviour
After data covered by a corrupted WAL segment exceeds the retention window, Prometheus could:
- Skip or discard corrupted WAL segments older than retention.
- Resume compaction on subsequent healthy segments.
- Optionally provide a configuration flag to enable this behavior (e.g. --storage.tsdb.ignore-old-corrupted-wal).

This would prevent unbounded disk growth while preserving the current safety-first default behavior.

# Rationale
Currently, WAL corruption results in a silent long-term failure mode:
- The system keeps running.
- No further compaction occurs.
- Disk usage grows indefinitely.
- Operators may not notice until disk exhaustion occurs.

Allowing Prometheus to automatically ignore/discard corrupted WAL segments once they fall outside retention would improve operational robustness without risking loss of in-retention data.

title: Add `max_firing_for` property on alert rules
body:
### Proposal

Hi,

# Goal

I'm trying to **downgrade the severity of an alert** for a given period.

# Context

In a kubernetes cluster, I have a redis cluster very susceptible to node deletion caused by spot instance interruptions and that triggers alerts because redis takes time to automatically recover (more than other more sensitive statefulset I have in the same k8s cluster). Here is the alert rule triggered by the flaky redis cluster:

```yaml
  - alert: k8s_statefulset_not_ready
    expr: |-
      (avg(kube_statefulset_status_replicas_ready / kube_statefulset_status_replicas_current * 100) by (namespace, statefulset) == 0)
    for: 2m
    labels:
      severity: critical
```

Since the kubernetes cluster is considered production, notifications are being sent to on-call engineers for `critical` alerts.

In order to stop notifying on-call for this redis-cluster I have setup the following alert rules which aim to serve a source alert rule in alertmagager's inhibit rules system:

```yaml
  # Redis StatefulSets can be flaky so we override the severity to warning during 5 minutes.
  - alert: k8s_statefulset_not_ready
    expr: |-
      (avg(kube_statefulset_status_replicas_ready{namespace="monitoting",statefulset=~"(redis-master|redis-replicas)"} / kube_statefulset_status_replicas_current * 100) by (namespace, statefulset) == 0)
    for: 2m
    labels:
      severity: warning
      severity_override: critical
```

The alertmanager inhibit_rule is the following:

```yaml
inhibit_rules:
- name: severity_override_critical_inhibit
  equal:
  - alertname
  - namespace
  - statefulset
  source_matchers:
  - severity_override = critical
  target_matchers:
  - severity = critical
  - severity_override = ""
```

This works well, on-call is no longer being notified when the susceptible redis-cluster is recovering, however, since the source and target alerts use the same rule expr logic **the warning alert will inhibit the critical alert ad-eternam**.

# Proposal

I'd like to have a mechanism that would allow to define a maximum duration an alert can be firing. With that mechanism it would be possible to expire source inhibition alerts after a certain amount of time and trigger the overridden target alerts.

```yaml
- alert: k8s_statefulset_not_ready
  expr: |-
    (avg(kube_statefulset_status_replicas_ready{namespace="monitoting",statefulset=~"(redis-master|redis-replicas)"} / kube_statefulset_status_replicas_current * 100) by (namespace, statefulset) == 0)
  for: 2m
  max_firing_for: 5m
  labels:
    severity: warning
    severity_override: critical
```

With `for: 2m` and `max_firing_for: 5m` the timeline would look like this:

- `0m`: statefulset crashes
- `0m`:
  - `alerts{name="k8s_statefulset_not_ready",statefulset="redis-master",severity="critical"}` **pending**
  - `alerts{name="k8s_statefulset_not_ready",statefulset="redis-master",severity="warning",severity_override="critical"}` **pending**
- `2m`:
  - `alerts{name="k8s_statefulset_not_ready",statefulset="redis-master",severity="critical"}` **firing (inhibited)**
  - `alerts{name="k8s_statefulset_not_ready",statefulset="redis-master",severity="warning",severity_override="critical"}` **firing**
- `7m`:
  - `alerts{name="k8s_statefulset_not_ready",statefulset="redis-master",severity="critical"}` **firing**
  - `alerts{name="k8s_statefulset_not_ready",statefulset="redis-master",severity="warning",severity_override="critical"}` **inactive(?)**

Regards.
