title: bug(sending RW2): RW2 sends disconnected exemplars without samples
body:
**Current implementation of the RW2 sending does not implement exemplars correctly.** It keeps the RW1 way of exemplars, where they are sent in a separate `TimeSeries` message with series labels, exemplar details and without samples. This represents the way Prometheus V1 Appender looks like and the current exemplar in-mem (and WAL) storage. We could call this model as "Exemplars per series".

However RW 2.0 spec follows more reliable way of exporting exemplars, so **have exemplar per sample**, similar to how our scrape protocols and OTLP have it. This is reflected in the following statement [in 2.0 spec:](https://prometheus.io/docs/specs/prw/remote_write_spec_2_0/#:~:text=At%20least%20one%20element%20in%20samples%20or%20in%20histograms%20MUST%20be%20provided.%20A%20TimeSeries%20MUST%20NOT%20include%20both%20samples%20and%20histograms.%20For%20series%20which%20(rarely)%20would%20mix%20float%20and%20histogram%20samples%2C%20a%20separate%20TimeSeries%20message%20MUST%20be%20used.)

> At least one element in samples or in histograms MUST be provided. A TimeSeries MUST NOT include both samples and histograms. For series which (rarely) would mix float and histogram samples, a separate TimeSeries message MUST be used.

However, the [current implementation does not represent this](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/e14795bbf4fbd1837a9e3428aafb40b4b1dda99d/storage/remote/queue_manager.go#L2001) logic as it takes incoming exemplars from WAL and send it as it is, in separate `TimeSeries` messages without samples. With sharding this might even mean totally separate RW request vs corresponding samples.

Seems this change is something that has been missed during RW2 sending implementation. This won't be easy to implement as well. Feels one solution is to do attack this problem similar to [the metadata problem](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/17191) e.g fetch time-relevant exemplars (or simply latest?) from the storage (what if storage is turned off)?

### Acceptance Criteria

* [ ] Fix exemplars RW2 sending to match the 2.0 spec
* [ ] Update RW 2.0 to be more clear on this important change -- it's easy to miss

### Alternatives

This missed change is something that likely current early adopters of RW2 missed too (e.g. Mimir, Otel Collector cc @ArthurSens ). It's late to change spec, but we could consider reverting this change RW 2.0 (make exemplars per series). I would vote for NOT doing this given:

* We wanted to limit spec changes at this point especially that big to 2.0
* It gets RW2 back to the stateful receiving for backends that store exemplars per sample (e.g. Google, OTLP). 
* For receivers that implement per series, switching RW2 implementation to be according to spec (exemplar per sample) should be noop.

The risk is that this issue will be for longer, so Prometheus sending RW2 won't support exemplars well until then.

title: NHCB: Disappearing bucket in input data leads to different result compared to pure classic histograms
body: ### What did you do? Enabled NHCB conversion globally and use a recording rule to pre-compute p50 latency from classic histograms aggregated across multiple application instances. ```yaml global: scrape_interval: 15s evaluation_interval: 15s convert_classic_histograms_to_nhcb: true scrape_native_histograms: true ``` **Recording rule definition:** ```yaml - record: http_request_duration_seconds_bucket:rate1m:sum_by_app:quantiles expr: | histogram_quantile(0.50, sum by(environment, datacenter, app) ( rate(http_request_duration_seconds{ controller!~"HealthCheck.*|Internal::.*" }[1m]) ) ) labels: quantile: "0.50" ``` The underlying `http_request_duration_seconds` histograms are classic histograms scraped from multiple application servers. Those are generated via the Ruby on Rails [Yabeda](https://github.com/yabeda-rb/yabeda) gem plus [yabeda-prometheus-mmap](https://github.com/yabeda-rb/yabeda-prometheus-mmap) Note: the recording rule name still contains the _bucket suffix for backward compatibility, but that will eventually be removed ### What did you expect to see? Stable p50 latency values around 0.013-0.016 seconds (13-16ms), consistent with the underlying request latency distribution. I understand that Native HIstograms are dynamic and we should be more careful while aggregating them, but my expectation is that NHCB have fixed boundaries coming from the original classic histograms, so aggregating multiple controllers that have the same original setup should work ### What did you see instead? Under which circumstances? Sporadic drops in p50 correlating with anomalous `histogram_count` spikes. Both come from the same native histogram. A separate `http_requests_total` counter (not derived from the histogram) remains stable, confirming actual traffic didn't change. **To isolate the issue, I filtered the recording rule output to a single app/datacenter/environment combination and compared against equivalent queries with matching filters and aggregation:** - Filter: `app="myapp", datacenter="dc1", environment="production", controller!~"HealthCheck.*|..."` - Aggregation: `sum by(environment, datacenter, app)` **Drop 1 (1768393500):** | Timestamp | p50 (s) | histogram_count | request_total | |-----------|---------|-----------------|---------------| | 1768393380 | 0.0127 | 1,279 | 1,250 | | 1768393440 | 0.0150 | 1,095 | 1,093 | | 1768393500 | **0.0027** | **65,450** | 1,051 | | 1768393560 | 0.0155 | 1,104 | 1,108 | | 1768393620 | 0.0152 | 1,165 | 1,167 | **Drop 2 (1768391160/1768391280):** | Timestamp | p50 (s) | histogram_count | request_total | |-----------|---------|-----------------|---------------| | 1768391100 | 0.0159 | 798 | 821 | | 1768391160 | 0.0157 | **9,840** | 851 | | 1768391220 | 0.0156 | 858 | 842 | | 1768391280 | 0.0167 | **18,763** | 943 | | 1768391340 | 0.0156 | 866 | 877 | **Drop 3 (1768392840):** | Timestamp | p50 (s) | histogram_count | request_total | |-----------|---------|-----------------|---------------| | 1768392720 | 0.0152 | 1,064 | 1,051 | | 1768392780 | 0.0139 | 1,181 | 1,161 | | 1768392840 | **0.0106** | **2,581** | 1,157 | | 1768392900 | 0.0140 | 1,121 | 1,157 | | 1768392960 | 0.0144 | 1,090 | 1,108 | - `histogram_count`: normal ~800-1,200/min, spikes 2x-60x during drops - `request_total`: stable ~850-1,250 req/s throughout (actual traffic unchanged) I used an AI agent to correlate the underlying raw NHCB data with the Prometheus code and the analysis is available [here](https://gist.github.com/B0go/268d09040bfcd9d91c5030e147a7dbe4), and I also compiled the raw series data [here](https://gist.github.com/B0go/9de2a77f489f7dca5dbde7a5f9d4610a) If it would help debugging, I'm happy to provide additional data, test patches, or enable debug logging. ### System information Linux 5.15.0-69-generic

title: PromQL: Refactor parser to use instance configuration instead of global flags
body:
The PromQL parser currently uses global package variables for configuration (`EnableExperimentalFunctions`, `ExperimentalDurationExpr`, `EnableExtendedRangeSelectors`). This causes several issues:

- **Not thread-safe**: Cannot have multiple parsers with different configurations
- **Fragile code**: Requires careful save/restore patterns
- **Hard to test**: Global state leaks between tests
- **Poor encapsulation**: Parser behavior depends on mutable global variables

### Proposal

Create a proper `Parser` struct with configuration and attach it to the PromQL Engine:

1. Add a `ParserConfig` struct holding all parser options
2. Create an exported `Parser` struct (currently there's only lowercase `parser`) with config
3. Attach a `Parser` instance (or parser factory) to the PromQL Engine
4. Initialize from feature flags once at startup in `main.go`

Example:

```go
// Create parser with config
parserOpts := parser.Options{
    EnableExperimentalFunctions: true,
    ExperimentalDurationExpr: true,
    EnableExtendedRangeSelectors: true,
}

// Engine holds parser configuration
queryEngine := promql.NewEngine(promql.EngineOpts{
    Parser: parser.New(parserOpts),
})
```

The engine would use its parser configuration when parsing queries.

### Benefits

- Thread-safe parser configuration
- No more defer/restore patterns in tests
- Clear ownership and better encapsulation
- Easier to extend with new options
- More flexible for future use cases

title: textparse: Move scrape.isSeriesPartOfFamily to text parser and optimize
body:
### Problem

Currently OM/Text (not proto!) `Type` `Unit` and `Help` parser methods can yield wrong metadata (belonging to a different metric family) for text formats for the cases like this (unknown metadata):

```
# TYPE test_metric3 gauge
# HELP test_metric3 this represents tricky case of "broken" text that is not trivial to detect.
test_metric3_metric4{foo="bar"} 2
```

Text and OM parsers would return `# TYPE test_metric3 gauge` metadata for `test_metric3_metric4` series.

This is reflected by the following unit tests: https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/main/model/textparse/promparse_test.go#L56

This functionally impacts:
* Metadata API
* type-and-unit-labels

We try to mitigate this problem for `metadata-wal-records` feature with [the funky `isSeriesPartOfFamily`](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/c021f316ba7d10852a85fd3d4616ccbc78f44523/scrape/scrape.go#L1833), but it's quite expensive (you need to find __name__ and check trillion suffixes).

It's getting bit more expensive for AppenderV2 flow too for `metadata-wal-records`: https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/17867#discussion_r2705178947

NOTE: This path will be also cheaper with OpenMetrics 2.0 because of metric family == metric name notion.

### Acceptance Criteria

* [ ] Handle this text/OM1 case in the text and OM parser.

title: Native Stateset in Prometheus
body:
### Proposal

### Context

OpenMetrics 1.0 defines the [Stateset](https://github.com/prometheus/OpenMetrics/blob/main/specification/OpenMetrics.md#stateset) metric type for enums-like and bitset-like data, so

```
kube_pod_status_phase{namespace="default",pod="nginx-7cdbd8cdc9-k8f9l",kube_pod_status_phase="Pending"} 0
kube_pod_status_phase{namespace="default",pod="nginx-7cdbd8cdc9-k8f9l",kube_pod_status_phase="Running"} 1
kube_pod_status_phase{namespace="default",pod="nginx-7cdbd8cdc9-k8f9l",kube_pod_status_phase="Succeeded"} 0
kube_pod_status_phase{namespace="default",pod="nginx-7cdbd8cdc9-k8f9l",kube_pod_status_phase="Failed"} 0
kube_pod_status_phase{namespace="default",pod="nginx-7cdbd8cdc9-k8f9l",kube_pod_status_phase="Unknown"} 0
```

Currently it's stored as normal gauges in Prometheus, which is prone to scrape inefficiencies, transactionality/atomicity problems on storage and long term storage ingestion.

We are at the moment of releasing OpenMetrics 2.0, where we introduce composite types in the text format. We [could make stateset a composite type](https://github.com/prometheus/OpenMetrics/issues/310) too e.g. 

```
# TYPE foo stateset
kube_pod_status_phase{namespace="default",pod="nginx-7cdbd8cdc9-k8f9l"} {states:["Pending":0,"Running":1,"Succeeded":0,"Failed":0,"Unknown":0]}
```

However, it's hard to make this decision and agree on a good enough format. Ideally text format is "what you see is what you query" but we never discussed how PromQL UX for potential stateset would look like. We rarely see stateset being used in practice. I see it only in Kube State Metrics project. 

**This ticket is to start the discussion about native stateset in TSDB**

### Questions

1. Is stateset a definitive answer to `string typed metrics` discussed a lot in the past? (https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/2227, https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/9139)

One thing that might be blocking some ideas there is that state can only be `0` or `1` whereas some use cases where mentioning any number (which is not allowed in the current OM 1.0 stateset). Allowing any number is a fun discussion because it would make it a `map` value really which moves cardinality to chunks/sample side (not indexed labels essentially).

2. Who uses statesets in prod? Please add emoji 👍🏽  or so to give us an idea and speak to us on Slack and KubeCons. We need user feedback on this!
3. Who wants to use them but can't? What's the adoption blockers, if any? Cardinality is one often mentioned item.
4. Would you prefer if we optimize StateSet in OM 2.0 for the future native use?
5. If we ever add native stateset to Prometheus, would that break OpenTelemetry compatibility (it's deprecated on Otel side). cc @dashpole @lyanco

Big discussion [happened recently on Slack too](https://cloud-native.slack.com/archives/C01AUBA4PFE/p1768480449294589)

promql: info() function incorrectly handles negated __name__ matchers
body:
### Bug description

The `info()` function incorrectly handles negated `__name__` matchers in the second argument. When using `__name__!~` or `__name__!=`, base metric series are incorrectly added to the `ignoreSeries` set and returned unchanged instead of being filtered out.

### Steps to reproduce

```promql
info(db_queries_total, {env="prod", __name__!~".+_info"})
```

### Expected behavior

Since no info metrics match `__name__!~".+_info"` (all info metrics end in `_info`), and the `env="prod"` matcher doesn't match the empty string, the query should return no series.

### Actual behavior

The query returns `db_queries_total` series unchanged (without any info labels added):

```
db_queries_total{instance="prod-db-1:5432", job="database", operation="UPDATE"}    1000
db_queries_total{instance="prod-db-1:5432", job="database", operation="SELECT"}    1000
db_queries_total{instance="prod-db-1:5432", job="database", operation="INSERT"}    1000
```

### Root cause

In `promql/info.go` (lines 50-60), series are added to `ignoreSeries` if their name matches any `infoNameMatchers`:

```go
for _, s := range mat {
    name := s.Metric.Get(labels.MetricName)
    for _, m := range infoNameMatchers {
        if m.Matches(name) {
            ignoreSeries[s.Metric.Hash()] = struct{}{}
            continue loop
        }
    }
}
```

The intent is "don't enrich info metrics with themselves". However, with negated matchers like `__name__!~".+_info"`:

1. `"db_queries_total"` does NOT match the pattern `.+_info`
2. The negated matcher `!~".+_info"` therefore returns `true`
3. `db_queries_total` is incorrectly added to `ignoreSeries`
4. Series in `ignoreSeries` are returned unchanged (lines 372-378)

### Suggested fix

The `ignoreSeries` logic should only consider positive matchers (`=` and `=~`), or the matching logic needs to be inverted for the purpose of determining which series to skip.

title: tsdb: Division by zero in stale series compaction ratio calculation
body:
## Bug Description

In `tsdb/db.go`, the stale series compaction threshold check performs a division that can result in division by zero when the Head has no series:

```go
numStaleSeries, numSeries := db.Head().NumStaleSeries(), db.Head().NumSeries()
staleSeriesRatio := float64(numStaleSeries) / float64(numSeries)
if db.autoCompact && db.opts.staleSeriesCompactionThreshold.Load() > 0 &&
    staleSeriesRatio >= db.opts.staleSeriesCompactionThreshold.Load() {
```

https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/main/tsdb/db.go#L1169-L1172

## Impact

When `numSeries` is 0 (empty Head):
- If `numStaleSeries > 0`: ratio becomes `+Inf`, which satisfies the threshold check and incorrectly triggers stale series compaction
- If `numStaleSeries == 0`: ratio becomes `NaN`, comparison returns false (safe, but semantically incorrect)

## Suggested Fix

Add a guard to skip the check when there are no series:

```go
numStaleSeries, numSeries := db.Head().NumStaleSeries(), db.Head().NumSeries()
if db.autoCompact && numSeries > 0 && db.opts.staleSeriesCompactionThreshold.Load() > 0 {
    staleSeriesRatio := float64(numStaleSeries) / float64(numSeries)
    if staleSeriesRatio >= db.opts.staleSeriesCompactionThreshold.Load() {
        // ...
    }
}
```

otlptranslator: Error silently swallowed in addSumNumberDataPoints
body:
## Bug Description

In `storage/remote/otlptranslator/prometheusremotewrite/number_data_points.go`, the `addSumNumberDataPoints` function silently swallows errors from `createAttributes`:

```go
lbls, err := c.createAttributes(
    pt.Attributes(),
    settings,
    nil,
    true,
    meta,
    model.MetricNameLabel,
    meta.MetricFamilyName,
)
if err != nil {
    return nil  // BUG: should be "return err"
}
```

https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/main/storage/remote/otlptranslator/prometheusremotewrite/number_data_points.go#L88-L89

Compare with `addGaugeNumberDataPoints` in the same file which correctly returns the error:

```go
if err != nil {
    return err
}
```

https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/main/storage/remote/otlptranslator/prometheusremotewrite/number_data_points.go#L47-L48

## Impact

When `createAttributes` fails for sum metrics, the error is silently discarded and processing continues. This could lead to:
- Silent data loss (sum metrics not being written)
- Difficult-to-debug issues in OTLP ingestion pipelines

## Root Cause

The bug was introduced in #16951 during a refactor. The original code had `return err`, but it was accidentally changed to `return nil`.

## Suggested Fix

```diff
 if err != nil {
-    return nil
+    return err
 }
```

body:
## Summary

The `DELETE /api/v1/series` endpoint has been non-functional since Prometheus v2.0.0 (November 2017), yet it remains registered in the API router. When called, it returns an HTTP 500 error with "not implemented".

Endpoint registered:

https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/dc34b90f93bf0265187ccec1dabdcc3db1a87ce0/web/api/v1/api.go#L1038-L1039

## History

Deprecated in PR #2910 (commit ccf9e6297206ab26d6051daf81f84d09b6bcd3b9) on July 6, 2017.

Replacement: Admin API endpoint `POST /api/v1/admin/tsdb/delete_series`

## Proposed Solution

Remove the endpoint entirely. It has been dead code for 7+ years and provides an unhelpful error message to users.

title: test: TestHeadCompactionWhileScraping is flaky
body:
## What happened?

`TestHeadCompactionWhileScraping` is flaky and can fail in CI with "Condition never satisfied".

Example failure: https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/actions/runs/21449194089/job/61773140350?pr=17740

```
--- FAIL: TestHeadCompactionWhileScraping (0.00s)
    --- FAIL: TestHeadCompactionWhileScraping/0 (15.12s)
        Error Trace:    /__w/prometheus/prometheus/cmd/prometheus/main_test.go:848
        Error:          Condition never satisfied
```

## Root cause

The test waits for at least 3 compactions to occur within the `require.Eventually` timeout:

```go
// Wait for some compactions to run
compactions, err := getMetricValue(t, bytes.NewReader(metrics), model.MetricTypeCounter, "prometheus_tsdb_compactions_total")
if err != nil {
    return false
}
if compactions < 3 {
    return false
}
```

This is timing-dependent and can fail in slow CI environments where compactions may not complete quickly enough.

## Possible fixes

1. Increase the timeout for `require.Eventually`
2. Reduce the number of required compactions
3. Use shorter `min-block-duration` to trigger compactions faster
4. Mark the test with appropriate skip conditions for slow environments

title: PROM-60: Finding room for ST in RefSample
body:
This is to track the issue we had when experimenting with introducing ST to the core float sample structure we use for TSDB appends -> WAL -> head compact/wal watching for remote write.

The moment we add the field we have ~5-10% CPU overhead that does not show on CPU profiles. Perhaps CPU L-cache misses? If yes, where? 

See one-pager for current details: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1OOm6a27FttMPp1dgga2HIeXOsjzLl6DI2dnG_LldgnE/edit?tab=t.0

Related PRs:
* https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/17671
* https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/18000 

This blocks PROM-60 to some extend. The alternative is to duplicate RefSample (and same for histogram and float histogram) structs, but it's going to be extra 10k LOC to maintain and test, which we want to avoid.

### Acceptance Criteria

* We understand why the CPU overhead exists
* We make data-driven decision how to store ST per sample going forward (accept overhead vs separate structs vs optimizations that reduce the overhead)

When we recognize that a regex simply matches a number of alternate strings we delegate to `containsStringMatcher` which works by calling `strings.Index` repeatedly.

title: prombench: Is Prombench reliable enough? fix or document ignorable baseline
body: > NOTE: Prombench is implemented mostly in [test-infra](https://github.com/prometheus/test-infra) repo, but adding issue here for visibility, as we make decisions based on prombench in this repo. Prombench is relatively unreliable. With [the recent proposed updates to the dashboard](https://github.com/prometheus/test-infra/pull/937) that shows and the average percentages of the difference across core metrics it yields extra +/-~3% allocs/s, +/-~6% CPU use, +/-3% HTTP latency The unreliability yields wasted time on chasing non-existing issues (e.g. https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/18022), or it masks existing issues. What's funny, it tends to be the "PR" node that is mostly worse for some reasons (order of creation?) Perhaps it's the effect of exact average calculations vs the YOLO "it looks kind of good to me" look on a graph, and it was always there, but in this issue I'd like to see what we can do to either: * Understand and improve reliability (especially on CPU side) * If we can't improve, document and improve dashboards to show the typical variance and when (how long to wait) e.g. make the numbers white if within acceptable ranges. Some tips on what we see from profile are [here](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/18022#issuecomment-3861807883) and it suggests kernel page behavior with mmaps, but it's a long shot. ### Ideas A) To rule out accidental use of irrelevant commits, I propose we extend prombench start logic to always build both PRs from source by default: https://github.com/prometheus/test-infra/pull/940 B) Find current variance baseline and document, I can update dashboard PR for i C) Investigate deeper e.g. * Load we put to both * Run PMU (e.g. https://github.com/perfgo/perfgo) to understand what happens with the process that gets worse (e.g. on cache misses). ### Evidences I ran exact 1:1 Prometheus's via custom prombench scenario: https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/18036#issuecomment-3870073553 Both using `quay.io/prometheus/prometheus:{{ .RELEASE }}` From what I looked so far, the load on both Prometheus-es are equal (queries, samples/s) Yet the variance is clear

title: promtool: add query label-names subcommand
body:
### Proposal

promtool query labels requires a label name argument and returns label values by calling    /api/v1/label/<name>/values. There is no subcommand to query all label names from a Prometheus server. The server exposes /api/v1/labels and the go client library provides v1.API.LabelNames(), but promtool does not use it.

so here, users cannot list all available label names from the cli. They must use curl or the web UI.

What I am thinking of?
Add a promtool query label-names subcommand that calls api.LabelNames() and prints all label names returned by the server. Consistently, it should accept the same --start, --end, and --match flags that promtool query labels already supports.

Users can call /api/v1/labels directly with curl. This works but is inconsistent with the rest of the promtool query interface, which wraps every other label and series query endpoint except this one.

title: Eliminate query gaps when Prometheus is restarting in HA mode
body: ## Problem When a large Prometheus is running in HA mode (i.e. 2 identical Prometheus) and it needs to be restarted (for upgrades, etc), there can be a temporary gap in queries when the second Prometheus is restarting. How the gap? Take the above example. T1 is the time range when prom-1 is restarting, and T2 is the time range when prom-0 is restarting. When prom-1 is restarting, it has no data during T1 since it does not scrape until it has restored its state. As a result, when prom-0 is restarting during T2, any queries to these Prometheus are only served by prom-1, which shows a gap for T1. This lasts until prom-0 has completely restored its state and can serve queries again. Once both Prometheus are up, both Prometheus fill each other's data gaps. The local gap in each pod also messes up recording rules that look back into the past, example `sum(rate(metric[5m]))`. Since these rules run within the pod, fixing the query gaps when queries externally is not enough. We should fix this query gap and also fix the disruption to the rules. We need to solve 2 distinct missing data: the raw scraped data, the rule evaluation data. This issue is meant to be an overarching issues for the sub-issues attached.

title: Retroactively evaluate rules after WAL replay in conjunction with #17058
body:
**Problem**

See the parent issue that describes the problem in detail: https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/18073

The aim of this issue is to fix the gap in the rule evaluation data data when Prometheus is restarting.

**Proposal**

Once the step 1 https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/17058 is done (start scraping immediately after startup), we now have all the data to retroactively evaluate rules for the duration Prometheus was replaying WAL.

Once the WAL replay is done, before marking Prometheus ready and start accepting queries, we retroactively evaluate all the rules from the startup time till now() and store it in TSDB.

We will disable compactions during this period so that we can bypass the current rule of "cannot append samples before X hrs" (X=1h by default with 2h blocks). We will also not fire any alerts during this period, but maintain the alert state so that it can fire once Prometheus is ready if it is still active.

title: [LTS 3.5] Bump Go toolchain to 1.24.13 to fix Critical CVEs
body:
### What did you do?

Based on https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/releases , latest Prometheus 3.5.1 LTS was built with Go 1.24.11, which has a few CRITICAL/HIGH vulnerabilities as follows: 

- CVE-2025-68121 (Critical) - stdlib go1.24.12 / go1.25.5, fixed in 1.24.13 / 1.25.7
- CVE-2025-61726 (High) - stdlib go1.25.5, fixed in 1.25.6
- CVE-2025-68119 (High) - stdlib go1.25.5, fixed in 1.25.6
- CVE-2025-61731 (High) - stdlib go1.25.5, fixed in 1.25.6
- CVE-2025-61732 (High) - stdlib go1.24.12 / go1.25.5, fixed in 1.24.13 / 1.25.7

[EDITED]How Prometheus is affected by these vulnerabilities?

The two most outstanding ones are:

1. CVE-2025-68121 (Critical) — crypto/tls session resumption bypass
This is directly applicable. Prometheus's [exporter-toolkit](https://github.com/prometheus/exporter-toolkit) uses GetConfigForClient to [support hot-reloading of TLS configuration](https://github.com/prometheus/exporter-toolkit/blob/6080e5327b9d5dea8365e29790b54c10da892363/web/tls_config.go#L412) (see `exporter-toolkit/web/tls_config.go` — the `Serve` function). Specifically, GetConfigForClient returns a fresh *tls.Config by re-reading the TLS config file on each new connection. This is exactly the pattern described in the CVE: if an administrator rotates client CAs (e.g., removing trust for a compromised CA) by updating the client_ca_file, a previously-connected client could still resume its TLS session under the old, now-revoked CA trust. This undermines the Prometheus security model's assumption that "only trusted users have the ability to change the command line, configuration file, rule files."

2. CVE-2025-61726 (High) — net/url / net/http ParseForm memory exhaustion
This is applicable. Prometheus exposes HTTP API endpoints (e.g., /api/v1/query, /api/v1/query_range, /api/v1/series, etc.) that accept URL query parameters and form data. The Prometheus security model explicitly states: "It is presumed that untrusted users have access to the Prometheus HTTP endpoint." An untrusted user could send a request with a very large number of unique query parameters to exhaust server memory, causing denial of service. While the security model acknowledges DoS is a concern, this CVE introduces a new, previously-unmitigated DoS vector at the Go stdlib level that Prometheus cannot defend against without a Go version bump.







### What did you expect to see?

**Request:** Could we get a Prometheus 3.5.2 LTS release with the Go toolchain bumped to 1.24.13+ to address these CVEs? This would be a toolchain-only change (no Prometheus code changes), consistent with how 3.5.1 was released over 3.5.0.

title: promql: native histogram optimization incorrectly skips buckets when intermediate operators need them
body:
### Description
 The native histogram optimization `detectHistogramStatsDecoding` incorrectly enables bucket-skipping (`SkipHistogramBuckets = true`) for `VectorSelector`s even when intermediate operators in the AST require those buckets.
For example, in the query `histogram_count(m1 + m2)`, the binary operator `+` needs the buckets of `m1` and `m2` to correctly merge them (especially if they have different schemas or bucket boundaries). However, the current implementation of `detectHistogramStatsDecoding` walks up the path and, if it finds `histogram_count` anywhere above the selector, it enables the optimization, leading to incorrect results because the binary operator receives histograms without buckets.
### Repoduction Steps
 1. execute a query like `histogram_count(series1 + series2)` where `series1` and `series2` are native histograms.
 2. the result is incorrect or potentially causes issues in the binary operator because buckets were skipped at the storage/iterator level.

title: `promtool check config` ignores `--enable-feature` flags for PromQL experimental features
body:
### What happened

After the parser refactoring in #17977, `promtool check config` no longer respects `--enable-feature` flags for PromQL experimental features (e.g. `promql-experimental-functions`, `promql-extended-range-selectors`).

### Root cause

In `cmd/promtool/main.go`, the `CheckConfig` function creates a default parser with no features enabled:

```go
// cmd/promtool/main.go:622
rulesFailed, rulesHaveErrors := checkRules(ruleFiles, lintSettings.rulesLintConfig, parser.NewParser(parser.Options{}))
```

Before #17977, this code path called `parser.ParseExpr()` which read global flags that were set earlier in `main()`. Now that globals are replaced with per-instance options, this call site uses a fresh parser that ignores the user's feature flags stored in `promtoolParserOpts`.

### Expected behavior

`promtool check config --enable-feature=promql-experimental-functions myconfig.yml` should accept rules using experimental PromQL functions.

### Actual behavior

Rules using experimental PromQL functions are rejected with parse errors, even when the corresponding `--enable-feature` flag is passed.

### Fix

Pass `promtoolParser` (or accept it as a parameter) instead of `parser.NewParser(parser.Options{})`.

title: `promtool test rules` ignores `--enable-feature` flags when loading rule files
body:
### What happened

After the parser refactoring in #17977, `promtool test rules` no longer respects `--enable-feature` flags when loading rule files containing experimental PromQL syntax.

### Root cause

In `cmd/promtool/unittest.go`, the `testGroup.test()` method creates a `rules.ManagerOptions` without setting the `Parser` field:

```go
// cmd/promtool/unittest.go:252-258
opts := &rules.ManagerOptions{
    QueryFunc:  rules.EngineQueryFunc(suite.QueryEngine(), suite.Storage()),
    Appendable: suite.Storage(),
    Context:    context.Background(),
    NotifyFunc: func(context.Context, string, ...*rules.Alert) {},
    Logger:     promslog.NewNopLogger(),
    // Parser field is missing
}
```

The `rules.NewManager` then falls back to `parser.NewParser(parser.Options{})`, which has no experimental features enabled. Meanwhile, `tg.parser` (which does have the correct features) is only used for parsing expected samples (lines 485, 489) but not for loading the actual rule files.

Before #17977, the global `parser.EnableExperimentalFunctions` (etc.) was set in `main()` and respected by all `parser.ParseExpr` calls, including those inside the rules manager.

### Expected behavior

`promtool test rules --enable-feature=promql-experimental-functions test.yml` should load rule files that use experimental PromQL functions.

### Actual behavior

Rule files using experimental PromQL functions fail to load with parse errors.

### Fix

Add `Parser: tg.parser` to the `rules.ManagerOptions` struct initialization.

title: Native histograms: optimize counting native histogram series
body:
### Proposal

Idea from @roidelapluie : 

When PromQL counts native histograms series it should not decode all pieces of information in the related native histograms chunk. 

What we really need to know is: what's the timestamp of the sample and whether it's a staleness marker or not.

Find a way to optimize away full decoding of native histograms samples to speed up operations that do not need all data.

Count is selected as most obvious place to start. Other operations that come to mind are : count_over_time, absent, absent_over_time, group(), timestamp, first_ts_over_time, last_ts_over_time.

title: tsdb: propagate errors from chunk writing instead of panicking in handleChunkWriteError
body:
### Proposal

`handleChunkWriteError()` (`tsdb/head_append.go:2237`) panics when a non-`ErrChunkDiskMapperClosed` error occurs during chunk writing. This was flagged with a TODO:

> TODO(bwplotka): Propagate errors correctly, even when they are async. Panicking here do occurs from time to time and cause flaky tests with hidden root cause (unlocked mutexes when deferred closing). We didn't have evidences of prod impact though, yet.

The panic is problematic because:
- It causes flaky tests with hidden root causes (e.g., unlocked mutexes from deferred closing)
- In the async write queue path (`chunk_write_queue.go`), a panic kills the worker goroutine, which is a separate failure mode
- Errors should be propagated and handled gracefully rather than crashing

### Proposed changes

Replace `handleChunkWriteError` with proper error returns across the chunk writing call chain:

**Synchronous path:**
- `mmapChunks()` → return `(int, error)` instead of panicking via callback
- `mmapCurrentOOOHeadChunk()` → return error alongside `[]ChunkDiskMapperRef`
- `cutNewOOOHeadChunk()` → propagate error
- `mmapHeadChunks()` / `mmapHeadChunksInStripe()` / `mmapSeriesChunks()` → propagate and log errors
- Callers in `head.go`, `db.go` → handle returned errors (log + continue or return)

**Async path (write queue):**
- `processJob()` in `chunk_write_queue.go` calls the callback on the worker goroutine
- The callback should log the error instead of panicking

**Call sites using `handleChunkWriteError`:**
- `tsdb/head_append.go:2184` — `mmapCurrentOOOHeadChunk`
- `tsdb/head_append.go:2193` — `WriteChunk` callback in `mmapCurrentOOOHeadChunk`
- `tsdb/head_append.go:2218` — `WriteChunk` callback in `mmapChunks`
- `tsdb/ooo_head_read.go:111` — `ToEncodedChunks` error in OOO head read

**Files involved:**
- `tsdb/head_append.go` — `mmapChunks`, `mmapCurrentOOOHeadChunk`, `cutNewOOOHeadChunk`, `handleChunkWriteError`
- `tsdb/head.go` — `mmapHeadChunks`, `mmapHeadChunksInStripe`, `mmapSeriesChunks`
- `tsdb/ooo_head_read.go` — OOO chunk encoding error handling
- `tsdb/db.go` — callers of `mmapHeadChunks`
- `tsdb/chunks/head_chunks.go` — `WriteChunk` callback signature
- `tsdb/chunks/chunk_write_queue.go` — async `processJob` callback invocation

title: File descriptor leak on early return in writeMetaFile (tsdb/block.go)
body:
### What did you do?

In tsdb/block.go (function writeMetaFile), a file descriptor is opened with:

    f, err := os.Create(tmp)

There is an early return path that exits without closing f:

    return 0, err

Other error paths in the same function correctly use:

    return 0, errors.Join(err, f.Close())

but this specific early-return path does not close the file.

If the error condition triggers, the file descriptor is leaked.

### What did you expect to see?

The file descriptor should be closed on all return paths.

Specifically, the early-return path should mirror the existing pattern used elsewhere in the function, e.g.:

    return 0, errors.Join(err, f.Close())

This ensures no file descriptor leak occurs on error.

### What did you see instead? Under which circumstances?

An early-return path exits without closing the file descriptor.

If os.Create(tmp) succeeds but a subsequent operation fails before the explicit close is reached, the function returns without calling f.Close().

This results in a file descriptor leak on that error path.

title: Push query log, scrape failure log to an OpenTelemetry OTLP endpoint
body:
### Proposal

Support sending scrape failure logs and query logs directly to an OpenTelemetry OTLP log receiver endpoint.

The scrape failure log and query log can currently only write to a file on disk. This can be awkward and inconvenient, especially in containerised environments, requiring management of ephemeral storage, log rotation, ingestion into external logging systems, etc.

While it's possible to bridge these to an OpenTelemetry log stream using an otel-collector's log reader, processors, etc in a sidecar container, this takes a significant amount of extra configuration and requires ephemeral storage.

Ideally Prometheus should be able to directly push the query log and scrape failure log directly to an OTLP log endpoint. This can serve as a useful complement to the existing OpenTelemetry tracing support, especially if log/trace integration is added to record trace-ids with logged queries and scrapes.

Uses include:

* Directly receiving query logs and scrape failure logs into tools like Grafana Loki for analysis
* Directly exporting query and scrape failure logs to managed monitoring services
* Sending query logs and scrape failure logs to an OpenTelemetry collector, which can perform metric generation from logs and various transforms before routing to other receivers
* Sending query logs to an intrusion detection system
* Sending query and scrape failure logs to a system configuration management and monitoring agent for anomaly detection, statistical aggregation of query information etc.

Logging queries and scrape failures an OTLP endpoint should not interfere with the existing json file logs; it should be possible to enable the two features independently.

I do not - yet - propose to support direct OTLP push for all Prometheus logs. This would introduce some chicken/egg issues with logging the opentelemetry-go exporter's internal logs, amongst other things. This proposal only covers the files Prometheus currently writes as independent json logs.

See related: https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/17421

title: `text/plain` and `openmetrics` parsers panic on unquoted metric name inside braces (e.g. `{A}0`), crashing the collector
body:
### What did you do?

The Prometheus text format and OpenMetrics parsers panic when they encounter an
entry whose line starts with `{` and contains a bare (unquoted) identifier not
followed by `=`, such as `{A}0`. Because the scrape pipeline has no panic
recovery, this crashes the entire Prometheus process.

**Affected parsers:** `PromParser` (`text/plain`) and `OpenMetricsParser`
(`application/openmetrics-text`)

## Steps to reproduce

Stand up any HTTP endpoint returning this body with `Content-Type: text/plain`:

```
{A}0
```

Point a Prometheus instance at it. The collector crashes on the first scrape.

The panic can also be reproduced in isolation:

```
package main

import (
	"github.com/prometheus/prometheus/model/labels"
	"github.com/prometheus/prometheus/model/textparse"
)

// Run against unpatched code: panic: runtime error: slice bounds out of range [2:1]
func main() {
	p, _ := textparse.New([]byte("{A} 0\n"), "application/openmetrics-text", nil, textparse.ParserOptions{})
	p.Next()
	var lset labels.Labels
	p.Labels(&lset)
}
```

```
package main

import (
	"github.com/prometheus/prometheus/model/labels"
	"github.com/prometheus/prometheus/model/textparse"
)

// Run against unpatched code: panic: runtime error: slice bounds out of range [2:1]
func main() {
	p, _ := textparse.New([]byte("{A}0\n"), "text/plain", nil, textparse.ParserOptions{})
	p.Next()
	var lset labels.Labels
	p.Labels(&lset)
}
```


### What did you expect to see?

The parser returns a parse error from `Next()` and the scrape loop logs it and
continues normally, as it does for any other malformed metric line.


### What did you see instead? Under which circumstances?

`Next()` returns `(EntrySeries, nil)` — no error — because the corrupt offsets
are not detected at parse time. The panic is deferred to the subsequent
`Labels()` call:

```
goroutine N [running]:
github.com/prometheus/prometheus/model/textparse.(*PromParser).Labels(...)
    model/textparse/promparse.go:237
panic: runtime error: slice bounds out of range [2:1]
```


### Prometheus version

I'm able to reproduce this on `main`.

title: Document default values of min/max retention time for agent mode
body:
### Proposal

The default values of `--storage.agent.retention.min-time` and `--storage.agent.retention.max-time` are not mentioned on [this page](https://prometheus.io/docs/prometheus/latest/command-line/prometheus/). Default values are not set when command line parameters are parsed.

```go
agentOnlyFlag(a, "storage.agent.retention.min-time",
	"Minimum age samples may be before being considered for deletion when the WAL is truncated").
	SetValue(&cfg.agent.MinWALTime)

agentOnlyFlag(a, "storage.agent.retention.max-time",
	"Maximum age samples may be before being forcibly deleted when the WAL is truncated").
	SetValue(&cfg.agent.MaxWALTime)
```

However, there are default values defined [here](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/main/tsdb/agent/db.go#L55)

```go
var (
	DefaultTruncateFrequency = 2 * time.Hour
	DefaultMinWALTime        = int64(5 * time.Minute / time.Millisecond)
	DefaultMaxWALTime        = int64(4 * time.Hour / time.Millisecond)
)
```

title: Native histogram query performance degradation in 3.10
body:
Noticed degraded performance of Native Histogram queries after upgrading 3.10. Apparently the culprit is replacement of `FloatHistogram.Add` with `FloatHistogram.KahanAdd`. A [simple microbenchmark](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/18248) shows the latter being 2.5x slower than the former, also doing lots of allocations:
```
BenchmarkFloatHistogramAdd/Add
BenchmarkFloatHistogramAdd/Add-10         	   58792	     20013 ns/op	       0 B/op	       0 allocs/op
BenchmarkFloatHistogramAdd/KahanAdd
BenchmarkFloatHistogramAdd/KahanAdd-10    	   23900	     50263 ns/op	   29905 B/op	     241 allocs/op
```
While I understand the benefit of improved precision, the tradeoff seems just too painful.

title: main: Make main() reusable
body:
### Proposal

`cmd/prometheus/main.go#main()` is the entry point for the Prometheus binary.

For e2e , code-level tests (e.g. strictly the same process), there's nothing better than calling `main()` function as it captures all that Prometheus is doing.

We do have some tests that do this in a neat way ([TestMain](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/a73202012b30954afac494cd0626ea2eb7c3860d/cmd/prometheus/main_test.go#L66), [process call](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/a73202012b30954afac494cd0626ea2eb7c3860d/cmd/prometheus/main_test.go#L139)), but it's outside of process which:
* can leak processes
* is harder to use/understand/test/control/mock
* blocks microbenchmarking use case (local profiles, CPU/alloc measurements etc)

Recently I hacked `main()` for yolo microbenchmark with some success: https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/b52ca810d0e2c6279a79061b5709a7b719d49df2/cmd/prometheus/main_bench_test.go#L243

It would be nice if `main` is reusable for testing purpose. I propose we wrap our main into separate (example) `run(ctx, args, reg) error` function that would unlock using `run` in various tests and benchmarks.

Currently, DigitalOcean Service Discovery in Prometheus only supports Droplets. DigitalOcean also provides Managed Databases which are often used as scrape targets (e.g., via postgres_exporter or mysql_exporter).

I have implemented a new SD mechanism 'digitalocean_db_sd_configs' that allows discovering DigitalOcean Managed Database clusters.

**Key features:**
* Discovers all database clusters in a DO account.
* Supports pagination (handles the specific way DO API handles it for databases).
* Provides comprehensive meta labels:
    * `__meta_digitalocean_db_id`
    * `__meta_digitalocean_db_name`
    * `__meta_digitalocean_db_engine` (pg, mysql, redis, etc.)
    * `__meta_digitalocean_db_status`
    * `__meta_digitalocean_db_region`
    * `__meta_digitalocean_db_host`
    * `__meta_digitalocean_db_private_host`
    * `__meta_digitalocean_db_tag_<tagname>`

I have the implementation ready with tests and documentation updates. Opening a Pull Request shortly.

title: "Compaction failed" errors in Windows container when TSDB (Data directory) is stored in Docker volume
body:
### What did you do?

It appears that Prometheus has issues running in a Windows container when its Data directory (TSDB) is stored in a Docker volume. When the container is using "Process" isolation, Prometheus is unable to run "compaction" against its TSDB. I was unable to find any reports regarding this particular problem.

These errors are logged and TSDB stays "uncompacted" forever:

`time=2026-03-16T16:20:52.875+03:00 level=ERROR source=db.go:1219 msg="compaction failed" component=tsdb err="compact head: persist head block: rename block dir: rename data\\01KKVCWYJVA6GQK2FVTE7X2YBZ.tmp-for-creation data\\01KKVCWYJVA6GQK2FVTE7X2YBZ: The system cannot find the path specified."`

This problem doesn't occur when TSDB is *not* stored in a Docker volume or some other Docker mount.

I've tried to use Hyper-V isolation mode for that Windows container, but encountered another issue which I think is covered in [#14331](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/14331). Prometheus simply crashes when Hyper-V isolation is used and there is a Docker volume. To add to #14331, the problem occurs with local Docker volumes as well.

Due to these problems, it appears that it's not possible to persist TSDB data when Prometheus is running in a Windows container. And in fact it seems that Prometheus doesn't simply support running in Windows containers. And if it's true, it would be great to mention this in the documentation somewhere. Sorry if I'm missing something here.

### What did you expect to see?

My expectation is that Prometheus can be run within a Windows Docker container and persist data via volumes. I am operating under the assumption that Prometheus officially supports Windows container deployment.

### What did you see instead? Under which circumstances?

I see that Prometheus cannot persist TSDB data when running in a Windows container which makes it impossible to run it in Windows containers beyond testing scenarios.

title: Feature Request: Prioritize Head GC execution over new incoming read requests
body:
### Proposal

**Background / The Investigation:**
Hello! We recently investigated a severe degradation in our Prometheus instances and traced it down to how Head GC interacts with continuous heavy read queries. We found the problem by following multiple symptoms that led us closer to the root cause:

1. Increased RAM consumption leading to frequent OOMKilled events.
2. Hundreds of WAL segments piling up in `/prometheus/wal`, causing extremely long restart times (35+ minutes).
3. The metrics `prometheus_tsdb_head_min_time` and `prometheus_tsdb_compactions_triggered_total` stopped growing or grew much slower than they should.
4. Looking at `/debug/pprof/goroutine?debug=2`, we found the main tsdb goroutine consistently stuck with this stack trace:

```go
goroutine 901 [sleep]:
time.Sleep(0x1dcd6500)
	/usr/local/go/src/runtime/time.go:363 +0x165
github.com/prometheus/prometheus/tsdb.(*Head).WaitForPendingReadersInTimeRange(0xc000564008, 0x19c032ff300, 0x19c034b6a3f)
	/app/tsdb/head.go:1207 +0x2c
github.com/prometheus/prometheus/tsdb.(*Head).truncateMemory(0xc000564008, 0x19c034b6a40)
	/app/tsdb/head.go:1168 +0x1be
github.com/prometheus/prometheus/tsdb.(*DB).compactHead(0xc0004068c0, 0xcd8619ce00)
	/app/tsdb/db.go:1501 +0x17e
github.com/prometheus/prometheus/tsdb.(*DB).Compact(0xc0004068c0, {0x633c7f8, 0xc0005320a0})
	/app/tsdb/db.go:1326 +0x38e
github.com/prometheus/prometheus/tsdb.(*DB).run(0xc0004068c0, {0x633c7f8, 0xc0005320a0})
	/app/tsdb/db.go:1118 +0x356
created by github.com/prometheus/prometheus/tsdb.open in goroutine 60
	/app/tsdb/db.go:1036 +0x158d

```

After further investigation, we found out that it was long-running read queries from our alerting rules that kept blocking the GC, and we were able to pinpoint exactly which ones were responsible.

**The Problem:**
Currently, Head GC waits for ongoing read operations to complete (`WaitForPendingReadersInTimeRange`), but it does not block or throttle *new* incoming read requests. If a system is under constant heavy read load, the Head GC starves. Data keeps accumulating in RAM without being flushed to disk, WAL grows out of control, and eventually, the entire instance crashes due to OOM.

**Proposed Solution:**
We propose prioritizing Head GC execution to prevent unbounded memory growth. We believe it is much safer for Prometheus to block new read queries (resulting in temporary read timeouts) during a pending Head GC rather than letting the memory grow until the process crashes. Temporary read timeouts are a lesser evil compared to a complete node failure and data ingestion interruption.

**Steps to Reproduce:**
I do not have a rigid isolated reproduction scenario, but the issue can be reproduced by simulating the conditions we observed using the debugging info above:

1. Generate a continuous stream of high-throughput, long-range-spanning read queries against the Prometheus API (these don't have to be alerts, any continuous heavy querying will do).
2. Monitor the `prometheus_tsdb_head_min_time` and `prometheus_tsdb_compactions_triggered_total` metrics - observe that they stall.
3. Check `/debug/pprof/goroutine?debug=2` and observe the tsdb goroutine getting stuck in `WaitForPendingReadersInTimeRange`.
4. Observe the WAL segments rapidly piling up on disk and memory growing continuously until the instance hits an OOM.

title: scrape: optimize `convert_classic_histograms_to_nhcb` (moving the logic to each parser, ST improvement)
body:
### Context

The implementation of `convert_classic_histograms_to_nhcb` has trivial optimization opportunities, we know about when introducing this functionality, but we never had chances to document those. This ticket captures initial ideas and plan here for further discussion and contributions.

@MichaHoffmann shared a profile reflecting some CPU impact https://pprof.me/a12c990ef9bcc1c4d86e24009e1807d5/?profileType=profile%3Acpu%3Ananoseconds%3Acpu%3Ananoseconds%3Adelta

Notably we see
* Relabelling impact (simple rules), likely unrelated to nhcb.
* Some NHCBParser "CreatedTimestamp" impact, due to [parser](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/a9d90952bac6ff117cd0d99171bf631fc8a3dce2/model/textparse/nhcbparse.go#L321) always touching StartTimestamp/CreatedTimestamp and [known OM1 in-efficiency](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/14823). Typically for non NHCB route we only do this on certain features that require ST. We don't know the exact impact as things are wrapped - CT method is buffering things upfront. Especially for histograms it can be expensive, although it's more memory heavy.

### Some Optimizations

Generally all optimizations are related to [the recent blog post](https://prometheus.io/blog/2026/02/14/modernizing-prometheus-composite-samples/) that talks about **combining** cost.

1. (trivial) Consider NOT doing `StartTimestamp()` call [in nhcb parser](https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/a9d90952bac6ff117cd0d99171bf631fc8a3dce2/model/textparse/nhcbparse.go#L321) unless `st-storage` or `created-timestamp-zero-ingestion` are set, as per https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/issues/14823
1. Add `convert_classic_histograms_to_nhcb` logic directly to Proto parsing. We unnecessarily expand and combine histograms.
1. Ensure `convert_classic_histograms_to_nhcb` logic is directly added to OpenMetrics 2 parsing as it's composite type friendly too (same as proto).

NHCBParsers would be then used only for OM1 and text parse for compatibility.

title: `NewOAuth2RoundTripper` is unusable from external packages due to unexported `*httpClientOptions` parameter
body:
### What did you do?

`NewOAuth2RoundTripper` is exported but its fourth parameter is `*httpClientOptions`, an unexported type. This makes the function effectively uncallable from outside `github.com/prometheus/common/config` with a non-nil options argument, forcing downstream users to resort to reflection and unsafe pointer tricks to work around it.

Current signature:

```go
func NewOAuth2RoundTripper(
    oauthCredential SecretReader,
    config *OAuth2,
    next http.RoundTripper,
    opts *httpClientOptions,   // ← unexported type
) http.RoundTripper
```

I ran into this while working on the [Grafana Alloy](https://github.com/grafana/alloy/pull/5810) `pyroscope.write` component, where I needed to enable the HTTP client to work with h2c (HTTP/2 cleartext), and found no nice way to construct `OAuth2RoundTripper`.

### What did you expect to see?

Exported function `NewOAuth2RoundTripper` uses exported types as arguments

### What did you see instead? Under which circumstances?

Exported function `NewOAuth2RoundTripper` uses an unexported `httpClientOptions` as an argument making it dificult to construct.

title: promtool: debug output writes to stdout instead of stderr
body:
## Description

The `--debug` flag in `promtool test rules` writes diagnostic output using `fmt.Printf` to stdout. This can interfere with machine-parseable output (e.g., JUnit XML via `--junit-output`) and piped workflows.

## Affected Code

`cmd/promtool/unittest.go` — 6 `fmt.Printf("DEBUG: ...")` calls and 1 `fmt.Println(v.String())` call inside `if debug {}` blocks write to stdout instead of stderr.

## Suggested Fix

Redirect all debug output to stderr using `fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, ...)`, consistent with the existing error output pattern already used in the same file (e.g., line 78: `fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "  FAILED:")`).

This is a minimal, backwards-compatible change that keeps debug diagnostics separate from tool output without requiring any API or function signature changes.

title: promtool: `push metrics <url>` always suffixes the path in the url with `/api/v1/write`
body:
`promtool` allows pushing arbitrary metric files to a Prometheus compatible remote write endpoint. But only if the endpoint path ends with `/api/v1/write`.

The problem being that `/api/v1/write` is always appended to the url given to promtool.
`http://localhost:8080/my/ep -> http://localhost:8080/my/ep/api/v1/write`

Mimir specifically only accepts metrics on `/api/v1/push` and promtool currently does not allow any way to overwrite this aside from prefixing the default path.

The Path is always appended with the default path value "/api/v1/write".
https://github.com/prometheus/client_golang/blob/8f78afd82a7fa242c008ec04280a9a836ee28808/exp/api/remote/remote_api.go#L151

https://github.com/prometheus/client_golang/blob/8f78afd82a7fa242c008ec04280a9a836ee28808/exp/api/remote/remote_api.go#L81

But the API options include the `WithAPIPath` func which allows overwriting the default:
https://github.com/prometheus/client_golang/blob/8f78afd82a7fa242c008ec04280a9a836ee28808/exp/api/remote/remote_api.go#L101-L107

Would you consider either changing the behaviour of how the `<url>` path is handled to instead overwrite the default path or alternatively be open to a PR adding a new parameter allowing users to override the default path?

title: `EscapeMetricFamily` incorrectly preserves `:` in label names
body:
### What did you do?

When escaping label names, `EscapeMetricFamily` and `EscapeName` treat `:` (colon) as a
legacy-valid character and leave it unescaped. This is correct for **metric names**, but
wrong for **label names**. The Prometheus data model has always reserved `:` for metric
names only; it has never been valid in label names.

The result: a label named `app:instance-id` is rendered as `app:instance_id` under
`UnderscoreEscaping` (the default) instead of the correct `app_instance_id`.

---


## How to reproduce

```go
package main

import (
    "fmt"
    "log"
    "net/http"

    "github.com/prometheus/client_golang/prometheus"
    "github.com/prometheus/client_golang/prometheus/promhttp"
    "github.com/prometheus/common/model"
)

func main() {
    // Direct escaping — shows the bug in model.EscapeName
    fmt.Println(model.EscapeName("app:instance-id", model.UnderscoreEscaping))
    // Got:      "app:instance_id"   (colon preserved — BUG)
    // Expected: "app_instance_id"   (colon should be escaped for a label name)

    // HTTP endpoint — shows the bug in EscapeMetricFamily via promhttp
    counter := prometheus.NewCounterVec(
        prometheus.CounterOpts{Name: "requests_total", Help: "Total requests."},
        []string{"app:instance-id"},
    )
    prometheus.MustRegister(counter)
    counter.WithLabelValues("my-server").Inc()

    http.Handle("/metrics", promhttp.Handler())
    log.Fatal(http.ListenAndServe(":9090", nil))
}
```

```
$ curl -s http://localhost:9090/metrics | grep requests_total{
requests_total{app:instance_id="my-server"} 1
#              ^^^--- colon preserved, hyphen correctly escaped to _

$ curl -s -H 'Accept: text/plain; version=0.0.4; escaping=allow-utf-8' \
       http://localhost:9090/metrics | grep requests_total{
requests_total{"app:instance-id"="my-server"} 1
#               ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^--- verbatim original (correct for allow-utf-8)
```

---

## Affected escaping schemes

All schemes that go through `EscapeName` are affected wherever `isValidLegacyRune` decides
whether to leave a character in place:

| Scheme | Input `app:instance-id` | Got | Expected |
|---|---|---|---|
| `underscores` (default) | `app:instance-id` | `app:instance_id` | `app_instance_id` |
| `dots` | `app:instance-id` | `app:instance__id` | `app__instance__id` |
| `values` | `app:instance-id` | `U__app:instance_2d_id` | `U__app_3a_instance_2d_id` |
| `allow-utf-8` | `app:instance-id` | `"app:instance-id"` | `"app:instance-id"` ✓ |

`allow-utf-8` (`NoEscaping`) is not affected because it returns the name verbatim by
design.

---

## Comparison with the Python client

`prometheus_client` 0.24.1 gets this right. It defines two separate rune validators and
two separate escape entry points:

```python
# openmetrics/exposition.py:263
def _is_legacy_metric_rune(b, i):
    return _is_legacy_labelname_rune(b, i) or b == ':'   # colon OK for metric names

def _is_legacy_labelname_rune(b, i):
    return ('a' <= b <= 'z') or ('A' <= b <= 'Z') or b == '_' or \
           (b.isdigit() and i > 0)                        # NO colon

def escape_metric_name(s, escaping=UNDERSCORES): ...      # uses _is_legacy_metric_rune
def escape_label_name(s, escaping=UNDERSCORES):  ...      # uses _is_legacy_labelname_rune
```

Side-by-side output for `UnderscoreEscaping`:

| Input | Python (label) | Go (label) | Agree? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `app:instance-id` | `app_instance_id` | `app:instance_id` | **No** |
| `http.status:sum` | `http_status_sum` | `http_status:sum` | **No** |
| `my-metric-name` | `my_metric_name` | `my_metric_name` | Yes |
| `my_metric:name` | `my_metric_name` | `my_metric_name` | Yes |
| `my.metric.name` | `my_metric_name` | `my_metric_name` | Yes |

### What did you expect to see?

A label named `app:instance-id` escaped as `app_instance_id` under `UnderscoreEscaping`
— colon and hyphen both replaced with `_`, matching the legacy label name character set
`[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*`.

title: Support periodic DNS re-resolution for FQDN targets discovered via Consul SD
body:
### Proposal

In dynamic environments where services are accessed via FQDN (e.g., multi-tenant systems behind nginx), IP addresses frequently change due to instance rescheduling or migration.

In our setup, Prometheus uses Consul service discovery and targets are defined via FQDN. When the underlying IP changes, Prometheus does not re-resolve DNS for already discovered targets. As a result, targets become permanently DOWN even though they are healthy and reachable.

This behavior creates a significant operational issue:

- Monitoring becomes unreliable
- Alerts are triggered incorrectly
- Manual intervention is required to recover

We verified that:

- DNS updates correctly reflect new IPs
- Prometheus only re-resolves DNS when the target is rediscovered (e.g., after deregistration and ~6 minutes delay)
- Restarting Prometheus also restores correct behavior, as DNS is resolved again on startup

This demonstrates that DNS resolution is tied to discovery events and process lifecycle, rather than ongoing scraping.

In environments where IPs are ephemeral and FQDN is the only stable identifier, this limitation makes Prometheus difficult to operate reliably without additional workarounds.

title: Flexible Proxy Configuration for Scrape Targets
body:
### Backstory / Use Case

In our current Prometheus setup, we manage approximately 400 targets per job across 5 jobs, each corresponding to a different exporter. We intend to route traffic for most targets through a proxy (e.g., for compliance, network segmentation, or observability reasons). However, there are certain targets that must be excluded from proxying due to special networking or compliance requirements.

Currently:

- Proxy settings in Prometheus (`proxy_url`) can only be set per job in `scrape_configs`.
- All targets within a scrape job inherit the same proxy config.
- Exclusion or inclusion by pattern matching (such as labels, regex, or within JSON target files) is not possible.
- Defining exclusions based on hostname or IP range is not viable, as our targets are defined by names and do not follow consistent patterns.

### Feature Proposal

#### 1. Per-Target Proxy Control

- **Label or Regex-based Exclusion:**  
  Enable an option to exclude specific targets from using the configured proxy based on target labels or a user-defined regex pattern.
  - For example, in the `file_sd` JSON, allow specifying a label (e.g., `"proxy_exclude": "true"`), and have Prometheus skip proxying those targets.
  - Alternatively, support regex matching within target labels or names, to exclude targets dynamically.

#### 2. Global Proxy Configuration

- **Global Proxy Setting:**  
  Allow configuring a proxy globally for all scrape jobs/targets, with the possibility for job-level and/or target-level overrides.
  - This would greatly simplify configuration management when many jobs require the same proxy settings.

### Benefits

- **Fine-Grained Control:** Allows exclusion of specific endpoints from proxying without reorganizing scrape jobs or duplicating configs.
- **Scalability:** Reduces configuration overhead for large-scale Prometheus deployments with hundreds of targets and multiple jobs.
- **Flexibility:** Supports dynamic environments where target membership and requirements change frequently.

### Example Configuration Ideas

```yaml
scrape_configs:
  - job_name: 'example'
    proxy_url: 'http://my-proxy:8080'
    file_sd_configs:
      - files: ['targets.json']
    proxy_exclude_label: 'no_proxy'
# or
global_proxy_url: 'http://my-proxy:8080'

body:
We see a lot of memory allocated by `NewXORChunk`:

```
(pprof) list NewXORChunk
Total: 99.23GB
ROUTINE ======================== github.com/prometheus/prometheus/tsdb/chunkenc.NewXORChunk in tsdb/chunkenc/xor.go
   11.85GB    11.85GB (flat, cum) 11.94% of Total
         .          .     66:func NewXORChunk() *XORChunk {
    8.93GB     8.93GB     67:   b := make([]byte, chunkHeaderSize, chunkAllocationSize)
    2.92GB     2.92GB     68:   return &XORChunk{b: bstream{stream: b, count: 0}}

title: Prometheus (and later on thanos) should be able to process expressions containing external labels
body:
### Proposal

Hi,

Using prometheus at scale (we run prom under two level of thanos federation, sometimes three), we are regularly faced with a UX pain point where people try to query prometheus directly / one of the intermediate thanos, and mess up using the proper labels. For instance they will specify `prometheus="foobar"` in their query on the actual prometheus, which will return no data.

We were wondering what you would think about enabling prometheus (as a first step) to handle this natively.

I can see three levels of various implementations of this:

1. most naive: just strip any label that is currently defined as an external label.
  a. i.e. if I have `prometheus: foo` defined as an external label, I can query `up{prometheus="bar"}`, which will be rewritten to `up{}`. This obviously returns false positives.
2. strict matches: check against the value defined in the config, only allow strict matches
  a. i.e. if I have `prometheus: foo` defined as an external label, I can query `up{prometheus="foo"}` but not `up{prometheus=~"fo."}`
  b. I don't like this solution, but I'm mentioning it because I've read other places where only strict matches are allowed. Assuming that it's still true, that there is a technical justification for this, and that we want to match that behavior... here it is
3. actual match: just check against the value, allowing strict and regex match

Either of these solutions would be handle at query time on the fly, without actually writing the external labels to the metric (i.e. not changing the behavior on the actual metrics). I don't know off hand why we would implement 1 and 2 over 3, but it's cheap to list them as options.

Hopefully this makes sense. Is that something we would be open to implementing? Or accept a PR for?

Let me know if you have any question. And happy to read about any concerns / why this wouldn't be possible.
Thank you for your time!

title: fix: reduce chunkAllocationSize initial capacity to avoid multi-GB heap over-allocation
body:
## Problem

`NewXORChunk`, `NewHistogramChunk`, and `NewFloatHistogramChunk` all pre-allocate a 128-byte backing slice:

```go
const chunkAllocationSize = 128

func NewXORChunk() *XORChunk {
    b := make([]byte, chunkHeaderSize, chunkAllocationSize)  // always wastes 126 bytes
    ...
}
```

In large Prometheus instances this causes multi-GB wasted heap. From the pprof traces shared in #18502:

| Allocation site | Before | After (cap=header size) |
|---|---|---|
| `chunkenc.NewXORChunk` | 3.54 GB | 0.69 GB |
| `chunkenc.(*XORChunk).Appender` | 1.04 GB | 1.09 GB (+0.05) |
| **Net saving** | | **~2.79 GB** |

The `chunkCompactCapacityThreshold` constant already handles the case where capacity should be shrunk post-use; it is not related to the initial size.

## Fix

Start with the minimum capacity (equal to the header size) and let Go's `append` grow the slice naturally when data is first written. This avoids the 126-byte waste on every chunk that is allocated but never written to, or written only a little.

This affects four chunk constructors: `xor.go`, `xor2.go`, `histogram.go`, and `float_histogram.go`.

Closes #18502

title: Explore removing special grammar for @ modifier functions in favor of standard function parsing
body:
The current PromQL parser implementation introduces special grammar tokens and handling for certain functions used with the `@` modifier. This adds complexity, some duplication, and makes these functions behave differently from regular function calls.

An alternative approach could be to invert this design:

- Remove the special grammar handling for these functions so they behave like standard functions.
- Extend the existing `@` modifier parsing to support regular function call syntax.
- Apply filtering by function name within the `@` modifier handling, rather than encoding this logic in the grammar.

This could simplify the grammar and make function usage more consistent.

This is likely a non-trivial change and may require experimentation to evaluate feasibility and trade-offs. The goal here is to understand whether this direction has already been explored.

**Potential challenge:**

One concern is case insensitivity for keywords. For example, the following is currently valid:

```
foo @ START()
```

If `START` becomes a regular function call, we would either:
- Break existing usage that relies on uppercase `@` modifier calls, or
- Reintroduce special handling during function resolution to preserve this behavior.

This introduces potential backward-compatibility concerns.


_Originally posted by @juliusv in https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/pull/17877#discussion_r3093040848_

title: Query result contains unexpected series due to duplicate series ID in WAL
body: ### What did you do? This issue came from our Cortex deployment which is based on Prometheus release 3.6.0. But Cortex uses the same TSDB code from Prometheus. I ran a single query `cortex_ingester_memory_series` and the query result contains 1 series from another metric. ### What did you expect to see? I expect to only see metrics with `cortex_ingester_memory_series` name. ### What did you see instead? Under which circumstances? One series in the query result with name `kubelet_xxx` ### Investigation I tried to investigate what happened and caused this issue. I got the WAL files on the bad ingester and found out that the 2 series with different metric name share the same Ref Id. When replaying WAL files at startup, if two different series (with different label sets) share the same series ref (ID) in the WAL records, the TSDB head enters an inconsistent state: 1. Both series are added to the **postings index** under their respective `__name__` label values 2. But in the **head series map** (`stripeSeries`), the second series overwrites the first because they share the same ref This causes incorrect query results: querying metric A returns a series that actually belongs to metric B. #### Concrete example Two series in the WAL share ref `800000`: - `cortex_ingester_memory_series{...}` → ref 800000 - `cortex_ingester_tsdb_append_total{...}` → ref 800000 After WAL replay: - The postings list for `__name__="cortex_ingester_memory_series"` contains ref 800000 - The postings list for `__name__="cortex_ingester_tsdb_append_total"` also contains ref 800000 - The series map maps ref 800000 → `cortex_ingester_tsdb_append_total` (last write wins) When querying `cortex_ingester_memory_series`, the engine: 1. title: rules: wildcard selector without __name__ matcher forces entire group into sequential evaluation
body:
**What did you do?**

Enabled concurrent rule evaluation via `--enable-feature=concurrent-rule-eval` and `--rules.max-concurrent-evals=4`. Created two rule groups: one containing an alerting rule with a binary expression where one operand has no `__name__` matcher, and a control group with equivalent rules that all have `__name__` matchers:

```yaml
groups:
  - name: wildcard_poisons_concurrency
    rules:
      - record: job:up:sum
        expr: sum by (job)(up)
      - record: job:up:count
        expr: count by (job)(up)
      - record: job:up:avg
        expr: avg by (job)(up)
      - record: job:up:min
        expr: min by (job)(up)
      - record: job:up:max
        expr: max by (job)(up)
      - record: job:up:stddev
        expr: stddev by (job)(up)
      # Second operand {env=~"prod_.*"} has no __name__ matcher.
      - alert: HighDiskUsage
        expr: max({__name__=~"node_disk_.+_bytes_total"} and {env=~"prod_.*"}) > 1e15

  - name: control_group_all_concurrent
    rules:
      - record: instance:up:sum
        expr: sum by (instance)(up)
      - record: instance:up:count
        expr: count by (instance)(up)
      - record: instance:up:avg
        expr: avg by (instance)(up)
      - record: instance:up:min
        expr: min by (instance)(up)
      - record: instance:up:max
        expr: max by (instance)(up)
      - record: instance:up:stddev
        expr: stddev by (instance)(up)
      # Same intent but __name__ is present in the selector.
      - alert: HighDiskUsageNamed
        expr: max(node_disk_read_bytes_total{job=~".+"}) > 1e15
```

**What did you expect to see?**

The 6 recording rules are independent of each other — they all read the scraped metric `up` and write to distinct output names, so none references another's output. They should evaluate concurrently in a first batch.

The `HighDiskUsage` alerting rule contains `{env=~"prod_.*"}` which has no `__name__` matcher, so its dependencies cannot be statically determined — it could match output from any prior recording rule. It is correct to treat this rule as depending on all prior rules and evaluate it sequentially *after* the concurrent batch completes.

Expected evaluation order:
1. **Batch 1** (concurrent): the 6 independent recording rules
2. **Batch 2** (sequential): `HighDiskUsage`, after batch 1 finishes

**What did you see instead? Under which circumstances?**

The control group evaluates concurrently. The group with the bare label selector evaluates entirely sequentially — including the 6 recording rules that are independent of each other:

| Group | Rules | Group eval time | Sum of rule times | Concurrency factor |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `control_group_all_concurrent` | 7 | 0.0013s | 0.0031s | **2.40** (concurrent) |
| `wildcard_poisons_concurrency` | 7 | 0.0071s | 0.0066s | **0.92** (sequential) |

A concurrency factor > 1 means rules ran in parallel (rule sum > group wall time). A factor ~1 means sequential. The poisoned group gets no concurrency benefit despite the 6 recording rules being independent of each other.

This happens because `buildDependencyMap` in `rules/group.go:1157` returns `nil` for the entire group when any single `VectorSelector` has no `__name__` matcher:

```go
if nameMatcher == nil {
    indeterminate = true
    return nil
}
```

A `nil` dependency map causes `AnalyseRules` to skip dependency annotation entirely, so `SplitGroupIntoBatches` places every rule in the sequential bucket. One rule with a bare label selector poisons concurrency for the entire group, even for rules that are provably independent of each other.

Related PRs:
- #12946 — original concurrent rule evaluation implementation
- #15560 — bugfix for empty dependency map
- #16039 — added `{__name__=~"..."}` regex support but did not address missing `__name__`
- #17064 — ALERTS/ALERTS_FOR_STATE optimization, unrelated

**System information**

darwin 24.6.0 arm64

**Prometheus version**

Reproduced on both:

```

title: relabel.Config YAML marshaling drops explicit replacement: "" / separator: ""
body:
### What did you do?

Load a Prometheus config containing a relabel rule with an explicit empty replacement and/or separator, then ask Prometheus to report its loaded config:
```yaml
  scrape_configs:
  - job_name: example
    static_configs:
    - targets: ['localhost:9090']
    metric_relabel_configs:
    - target_label: test
      replacement: "" # <---
      action: replace
```

Now query the loaded config:
```bash
curl http://localhost:9090/api/v1/status/config | jq -r .data.yaml | grep metric_relabel_configs -A10
  metric_relabel_configs:
  - separator: ;
    target_label: test
    action: replace
```

### What did you expect to see?

The reported config should round-trip — the rule emitted by `/api/v1/status/config` should still contain `replacement: ""`, because missing field means "default" which is `$1` and not `""`
https://prometheus.io/docs/prometheus/latest/configuration/configuration/#relabel_config

### What did you see instead? Under which circumstances?

`replacement: ""` is missing from the output. The same applies to `separator: ""`:

```yaml
  metric_relabel_configs:
  - separator: ;
    target_label: test
    action: replace
```
  A reader of `/api/v1/status/config` cannot distinguish "user explicitly set `replacement: ""`" from "user did not set replacement (default `$1`)". Same for separator (`""` vs default `;`).

### Where is the bug?

https://github.com/prometheus/prometheus/blob/ecab2f45a8b7a1f12b8a16590a56590c96422f44/model/relabel/relabel.go#L86

```go
  type Config struct {
      ...
      Separator   string `yaml:"separator,omitempty"   json:"separator,omitempty"`
      ...
      Replacement string `yaml:"replacement,omitempty" json:"replacement,omitempty"`
      ...
  }
```

  The fields are plain `string` with `omitempty`, so the zero value `""` is dropped at marshal time. The runtime behavior is correct — `UnmarshalYAML` seeds the struct from `DefaultRelabelConfig` and lets explicit values overwrite, so an in-memory `Replacement = ""` is preserved and applied at scrape time. Only the re-serialization loses the distinction.

  This affects:
  - `/api/v1/status/config` (prometheus own web-UI)
  - any tool that need to save `*config.Config` to YAML (e.g. `promtool` workflows, downstream code that uses `model/relabel` as a library. I've hit this by writing own prometheus-controller).

  Suggested fix

  Switch `Replacement` and `Separator` to `*string` (or add a custom `MarshalYAML` on `Config`). Update `UnmarshalYAML` to populate the pointers from the inline plain-Config values, and update validators / consumers to dereference. This is the same shape `prometheus-operator` adopted to fix the equivalent bug at its layer:

  - https://github.com/prometheus-operator/prometheus-operator/pull/6451 (Replacement → *string)
  - https://github.com/prometheus-operator/prometheus-operator/pull/6425 (Separator → *string)
